chapters: And Shlomo the son of Dovid strengthened himself upon his kingdom, and Havayah his Elokim was with him, and He made him exceedingly great.
And Shlomo said to all Yisroel, to the leaders of the thousands and the hundreds and to the judges and to every prince of all Yisroel, the chiefs of the fathers' [houses].
And Shlomo and the entire assembly with him went to the high place that was in Givon, for there was Elokim's Tent of Meeting, which Moshe, the servant of Havayah, had made in the desert.
But Dovid had brought up the Ark of Elokim from Kiryas-Yearim in [the place that] Dovid had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Yerushalayim.
And the copper altar that Bezalel the son of Uri the son of Hur had made he placed before the Tabernacle of Havayah, and Shlomo and the assembly sought it.
And Shlomo offered up there on the copper altar before Havayah, which belonged to the Tent of Meeting, and he offered up on it a thousand burnt offerings.
On that night, Elokim appeared to Shlomo, and He said to him, "Request, what shall I give you?"
And Shlomo said to Elokim, "You performed great loving-kindness with my father Dovid, and You enthroned me in his stead.
Now, O Havayah Elokim, may Your word with my father Dovid come true, for You have enthroned me over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
Now, give me wisdom and knowledge, and I shall go forth before this people and come in, for who will be able to judge this great people of Yours?"

And Elokim said to Shlomo, "Since this was in your heart, and you did not request riches, possessions, and honor, neither have you requested the life of your enemies, nor have you requested many days, but you have requested for yourself wisdom and knowledge, that you should judge My people, over whom I have enthroned you.
Wisdom and knowledge are granted you, and riches, possessions, and honor I shall grant you, such as that the kings before you did not possess, and which will not be so after you."
And Shlomo, [who] had come to the high place, which was in Givon, [came] to Yerushalayim, from before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Yisroel.
And Shlomo amassed chariots and horsemen, and he had a thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he left them in the chariot cities and with the king in Yerushalayim.
And the king made the silver and the gold in Yerushalayim like stones, and the cedars he made as numerous as the sycamores that are in the lowland.
And Shlomo's source of horses was from Mitzrayim, and [there was] an assemblage, from which the king's agents would buy the assemblage privileges for a price.

And they brought up and took out of Mitzrayim a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty, and so to all the kings of the Chitim and the kings of Aram they would export through them.
And Shlomo ordered to build a House in the name of Havayah and a house for his kingdom.
And Shlomo counted seventy thousand who bore burdens and eighty thousand hewers in the mountains, and three thousand and six hundred were overseeing them.
And Shlomo sent to Huram the king of Tzor, saying, "As you did with my father Dovid, and you sent him cedars to build for himself a House in which to dwell.

Behold I am building a house in the name of Havayah my Elokim, to devote to Him, to burn before Him incense and the arrangement of the continual showbread and burnt offerings, for the morning and for the evening, for Sabbaths and for New Moons, and for the appointed seasons of Havayah our Elokim, making this permanent over Yisroel.
And the House which I am building is great, for our Elokim is greater than all gods.
And who can gather up strength to build Him a House, for the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain Him, and who am I that I should build Him a House, only to burn incense before Him.

And now, send me a wise man to work with gold, with silver, with copper, with iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue yarn, and who knows how to make engravings with the wise men who are with me in Yehudah and in Yerushalayim, whom my father Dovid prepared.
And send me cedar wood, cypress wood, and brazilwood from Levanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the trees of Levanon, and behold my servants are with your servants.
And to prepare for me abundant timber, for the House that I am building is large and wonderful.

And behold for the wood cutters, for those who cut the timber, I shall give abundant wheat for your servants, twenty thousand kors, and barley twenty thousand kors, and wine twenty thousand baths, and oil twenty thousand baths."
And Huram the king of Tzor said in writing, and sent to Shlomo, "Because of Havayah's love for His people, He made you king over them."

And Huram the king of Tzor said, "Blessed is Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, Who made the heavens and the Earth, Who gave King Dovid a wise son, endowed with intelligence and understanding, who will build a House for Havayah and a house for his kingdom.
And now, I have sent a wise man, endowed with understanding, of my father Huram.

The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a Tzori man, who knew how to work with gold, with silver, with copper, with iron, with stones, with wood, with purple, with blue, and with fine linen and with crimson yarn, and to engrave all types of engravings, and to devise ideas, [to do] what is given to him with your wise men and the wise men of my master, your father Dovid.
And now, the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine, which my master said, he shall send to his servants.
And we shall cut timber from Levanon, as much as you need, and we shall bring it to you as rafts on the sea of Yafo, and you will bring them up to Yerushalayim."

And Shlomo counted all the strangers who were in the land of Yisroel, after the census in which his father Dovid had counted them, and they were found to be one hundred fifty-three thousand and six hundred.
And he made of them seventy thousand who bear burdens, eighty thousand who hew in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers, to make the people work.

And Shlomo commenced to build the House of Havayah in Yerushalayim on Mount Moryah, where He had appeared to his father Dovid, which he had prepared in Dovid's place, in the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusi.
And he commenced to build in the second month, in the second, in the fourth year of his reign.
And [with] these Shlomo was counseled to build the House of Elokim; the length in cubits, in the first measure was sixty cubits, and the breadth was twenty cubits.
And the vestibule, the length of which was according to the breadth of the House, was twenty cubits, and the height was one hundred and twenty, and he overlaid it from within with pure gold.
And the greater House he overlaid with juniper wood, and he overlaid it with fine gold, and he wrought upon it palm trees and chains.
And he overlaid the House with precious stone for glory, and the gold was the gold of Parvaim.
And he overlaid the House; the beams, the sideposts and its walls and its doors with gold, and he engraved cherubim on the walls.

And he made the House of the Holy of Holies, its length on the face of the breadth of the House, twenty cubits, and its breadth twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with fine gold of six hundred talents.
And the weight of the nails in shekels, fifty of gold, and the upper stories he overlaid with gold.
And he made in the Holy of Holies two cherubim, with the appearance of children, and they overlaid them with gold.

And the wings of the cherubim-their length was twenty cubits, the wing of the one was five cubits, reaching the wall of the House, and the other wing was five cubits, reaching the wing of the other cherub.
And the wing of the one cherub was five cubits, reaching the wall of the House, and the other wing was five cubits, cleaving to the wing of the other cherub.
The wings of these cherubim were spread out twenty cubits, and they were standing on their feet with their faces to the House.
And he made the dividing curtain of blue, purple, and crimson yarn, and fine linen, and he wrought cherubim into it.
And he made before the House two pillars, thirty-five cubits long, and the capital that was on the top of each one was five cubits.
And he made chains in the Devir, and he placed [them] atop the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and placed them in the chains.
And he erected the pillars before the Heichal, one from the right and one from the left, and he named the right one Yachin and the left one Boaz.
And he made the copper altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
And he made the molten sea, ten cubits from brim to brim; it was round all about, and the height thereof was five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits did encompass it round about.
And the likeness of oxen was beneath it, round about, encompassing it; ten cubits encompassing the sea round about; the oxen were cast in two rows, when it was cast.
It stood on twelve oxen, three facing northward, three facing westward, three facing southward, and three facing eastward, and the sea was above them, and all their hind parts were inward.
And its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was like the work of the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies; it contained baths; it contained three thousand.

And he made ten lavers, and he placed five on the right and five on the left, to wash with them; the performance of the burnt offering they would rinse with them, and the sea was for the priests to wash therein.
And he made the ten golden candelabra according to their regulations, and he placed five in the Heichal, five from the right and five from the left.
And he made ten tables and placed them in the Heichal, five from the right and five from the left, and he made a hundred golden basins.
And he made the priests' court and the large court, and doors for the forecourt, and he overlaid their doors with copper.
And he placed the sea from the right side eastward opposite the south.
And Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the basins, and Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Shlomo in the House of Elokim.
Two pillars and the two bowls and chapiters atop the pillars, and the networks were two to cover the two bowls of the chapiters, which were atop the pillars.
And the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates to one network, to cover the two bowls of the chapiters, which were before the pillars.
And he made the bases, and he made the lavers on the bases.
The one sea, and the twelve oxen under it.
And the pots, and the shovels, and the forks and all their vessels, his father Huram made for King Shlomo for the House of Havayah, of burnished copper.
In the plain of the Yarden did Shlomo cast them in the thickness of the ground, between Succoth and Zeredathah.
And Shlomo made all these vessels of great abundance, for the weight of the copper was not found out.
And Shlomo made all these vessels, which were in the House of Elokim; the golden altar, the tables, and the showbread upon them.
And the candelabra and their lamps to kindle them as is required, before the Devir, of refined gold.
And the flower and the lamps and the tongs were gold, it was fine gold.

And the musical instruments, and the basins, and the spoons, and the censers of refined gold, and the entrance to the House, its inner doors to the Holy of Holies, and the doors of the House to the Heichal were gold.

Now all the work that Shlomo did for the House of Havayah was completed, and Shlomo brought his father Dovid's hallowed things, and the silver and the gold and all the vessels he deposited in the treasuries of the House of Elokim.

Then Shlomo assembled the elders of Yisroel and all the chiefs of the tribes, the princes of the fathers' [houses] of the Children of Yisroel, to Yerushalayim, to bring up the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah from the City of Dovid, which is Tziyon.
And all the men of Yisroel assembled on the festival; that is the seventh month.
And all the elders of Yisroel came, and the Leviim bore the Ark.
And they brought up the Ark and the Tent of Meeting, and all the sacred vessels that were in the Tent; the priests [and] the Leviim brought them up.
And King Shlomo and all the congregation of Yisroel, who were gathered with him before the Ark were sacrificing sheep and oxen that could not be counted or numbered because of their abundance.
And the priests brought the Ark of the Covenant of Havayah to its place, to the Devir of the House, to the Holy of Holies, to [the place] beneath the wings of the cherubim.
And the cherubim were spreading their wings over the place of the Ark, and the cherubim covered over the Ark and over its staves from above.
And they extended the staves so that the ends of the staves were seen from the Ark before the Devir, but they were not seen outside, and they were there until this day.
There was nothing in the Ark but the two tablets that Moshe gave in Horeb, when Havayah made [a covenant] with the Children of Yisroel when they left Mitzrayim.
And it came to pass when the priests left the Holy, for all the priests that were present had sanctified themselves; not taking heed of the divisions.

And the Leviim who sang — all of them, Asaf, Heiman, Yedusun, and their sons and their brethren, attired in fine linen, with cymbals and with psalteries and with harps, standing east of the altar, and with them were priests-one hundred twenty sounding with trumpets.

And the trumpeters and the singers were as one, to make one sound, to praise and to thank Havayah, and when they raised a sound with trumpets and with cymbals and with the musical instruments and with praise to Havayah, "for He is good, because His kindness is eternal," and the House became full of the cloud of the House of Havayah.
And the priests could not stand to serve because of the cloud, because the glory of Havayah filled the House of Elokim.
Then Shlomo said, "Havayah said that He would dwell in the thick darkness.
But I have built You a House to dwell in; a settled place for You to dwell in forever."
And the king turned his face about and blessed all the congregation of Yisroel, and all the congregation of Yisroel stood.
And he said, "Blessed be Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, Who spoke with His mouth to Dovid my father, and has fulfilled it with His hand, saying:

Since the day that I brought My people forth from the land of Mitzrayim, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Yisroel to build a House, that My name might be therein, neither did I choose a man to be prince over My people Yisroel.
And I chose Yerushalayim that My name might be there, and I chose Dovid to be over My people Yisroel.
And it was in my father Dovid's heart [the desire] to build a House for the name of Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel.
And Havayah said to Dovid my father; Since it was in your heart to build a House to My name, you did well that it was in your heart.
Nevertheless, you shall not build the House, but your son who will come forth out of your loins he shall build the House for My name.

And Havayah has established His word that He spoke, and I have risen up in the place of Dovid my father, and I have sat on the throne of Yisroel, as Havayah spoke, and I have built the House for the name of Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel.
And I have set there the Ark, wherein is the Covenant of Havayah, which He made with the Children of Yisroel."
And he stood before the altar of Havayah opposite all the congregation of Yisroel, and he spread forth his hands.

For Shlomo had made a copper laver, which he had placed within the forecourt, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and he stood on it and kneeled on his knees opposite all the congregation of Yisroel, and he spread forth his hands toward heaven.
And he said, "Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, there is no Elokim like You in heaven or on Earth, Who keeps the covenant and the kindness with Your servants, who walk before You with all their heart.
For You have kept for Your servant Dovid my father that which You spoke to him, and You spoke with Your mouth and fulfilled it with Your hand, as [it is] this day.

And now, O Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, keep for Your servant, Dovid my father, that which You spoke to him, saying, 'You shall never lack a man before Me sitting on the throne of Yisroel, if only your children take heed to their way, to walk in My Law as you have walked before Me.'
And now, O Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, let Your word come true, which You spoke to Your servant, to Dovid.
But will Elokim indeed dwell with man on the Earth? Behold the heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You; much less this House that I have built.
And You shall turn to Your servant's prayer and to his supplication, O Havayah my Elokim; to hearken to the cry and to the prayer that Your servant is praying before You.
That Your eyes may be open toward this House day and night, toward the place in which You said that You would put Your name, to hearken to the prayer that Your servant will pray in this place.

And You shall hearken to the supplications of Your servant and of Your people Yisroel when they will pray toward this place; You shall hear from Your abode, from heaven, and You shall hear and forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath be exacted of him to cause him to swear, and he come and swear before Your altar in this House.
You shall hear from heaven, and do, and judge Your servants, to recompense the wicked, to bring his way upon his head, and to justify the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
And if Your people Yisroel is struck down before the enemy because they sin against You, and they repent and confess to Your name and pray and make supplication before You in this House.
You shall hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Yisroel and bring them back to the land that You gave to them and to their fathers.
When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess to Your name, and repent of their sin, so that You may answer them.

You shall hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your servants and Your people Yisroel, for You will teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and You shall give rain upon Your land, which You have given Your people for an inheritance.

If there be famine in the land, if there be pestilence, if there be blast, mildew, increasing locusts, finishing locusts, if their enemies besiege them in the land of their cities, whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness [there be].
Any prayer, any supplication, which will be [made] by any man or by all Your people Yisroel, every man shall know his plague and his pain, and spread forth his hands toward this House.
You shall hear from heaven, Your dwelling, and forgive, and give to each man according to his ways, whose heart You know, for You alone know the hearts of the children of men.
That they may fear You to go in Your ways all the days that they live on the face of the land that You gave our fathers.

And also to the stranger, who is not of Your people Yisroel, but will come from a distant land because of Your great name, Your strong hand, and Your outstretched arm, and they will come and pray toward this House.

You shall hear from heaven, from Your dwelling place, and You shall do whatever the stranger calls upon You, that all peoples of the Earth may know Your name, to fear You, as [do] Your people Yisroel, and that they may know that Your name is called upon this House, which I have built.
If Your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way You send them, and pray to You toward this city, which You have chosen, and the House that I have built for Your name.
You shall hear from heaven their prayer and supplication and maintain their cause.
If they sin against You, for there is no man who does not sin, and You will be angry with them and deliver them to the enemy, and their captors will carry them in captivity to a land, far or near.

And they bethink themselves in the land where they were carried off into captivity, and repent and make supplications to You in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned; we have dealt perversely, and we have committed wickedness.'

And they return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity where they led them away captives, and pray toward their land, which You gave to their fathers, and the city that You chose, and toward the House that I built for Your name.
You shall hear from heaven, from Your dwelling place, their prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause, and You shall forgive Your people who sinned against You.
Now, my Elokim, may Your eyes now be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.

And now, arise, O Havayah Elokim to Your resting place, You and the Ark of Your might; Your priests, O Havayah Elokim, shall be attired with salvation, and Your pious ones shall rejoice with the goodness.
O Havayah Elokim, do not turn back the face of Your anointed one; remember the kind deeds of Dovid Your servant."
And when Shlomo finished praying, and the fire descended from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the glory of Havayah filled the House.
And the priests could not enter the House of Havayah, because the glory of Havayah filled the House of Havayah.

And all the Children of Yisroel saw the descent of the fire, and the glory of Havayah on the House, and they kneeled on their faces to the ground on the floor, and they prostrated themselves and [said]: "Give thanks to Havayah, for He is good, for His loving-kindness is eternal."
And the king and all the people were slaughtering sacrifices before Havayah.
And King Shlomo slaughtered the sacrifices of cattle, twenty-two thousand, and sheep, one hundred and twenty thousand, and they dedicated the House of Elokim, the king and all the people.

And the priests were standing on their watches, and the Leviim with the instruments of the song of Havayah, which King Dovid had made to give thanks to Havayah, for His loving-kindness is eternal, with Dovid's praise in their hand; and the priests were sounding the trumpets opposite them, and all Yisroel were standing.

And Shlomo consecrated the interior of the court that was before the House of Havayah, for there he offered up the burnt offerings and the fats of the peace offerings, for the copper altar that Shlomo had made could not contain the burnt offerings, the meal offerings, and the fats.
Now Shlomo observed the Feast at that time seven days, and all Yisroel with him, a very great assemblage from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Mitzrayim.
And they made on the eighth day a solemn gathering, for the inauguration of the altar they made seven days, and the feast seven days.

And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he dismissed the people to their homes, rejoicing and delighted of heart for all the goodness that Havayah had wrought for Dovid, for Shlomo, and for Yisroel His people.
And Shlomo completed the House of Havayah and the king's palace and whatever entered Shlomo's mind to make in the House of Havayah and in his palace, he succeeded.
And Havayah appeared to Shlomo at night, and He said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for Myself for a House of sacrifice.
If I shut up the heaven and there be no rain, and if I command locusts to devour the land, or if I send pestilence upon My people.
And My people, upon whom My name is called, humble themselves and pray and seek My presence and repent of their evil ways, I shall hear from heaven and forgive their sin and heal their land.
Now, My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
And now, I have chosen and consecrated this House that My name be there forever, and My eyes and heart will be there at all times.
As for you, if you walk before Me as your father Dovid walked, and do according to all that I commanded you, and you keep My statutes and My ordinances.
I shall set up the throne of your kingdom as I decreed to your father Dovid, saying: You shall never lack a man ruling in Yisroel.
But if you revert and forsake My statutes and My commandments, which I placed before you, and you go and worship strange gods and prostrate yourselves to them.

I shall uproot them from upon My land, which I gave them, and this House, which I have consecrated for My name I shall cast from before Me, and I shall make it a proverb and a byword among all peoples.
And this House, which was exalted, every passerby will be astounded, and they will say: Why has Havayah done this to this country and to this Temple?

And they will be told: Because they forsook Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers, Who took them out of the land of Mitzrayim, and they adopted strange gods and prostrated themselves to them and worshiped them; therefore, He brought upon them all this evil."
Now it came to pass at the end of twenty years that Shlomo had built the House of Havayah and his palace.
And the cities that Huram had given to Shlomo, Shlomo built them and settled Yisroelim there.
And Shlomo went to Hamath of Zobah, and he besieged it.
And he built Tadmor in the desert and all the store cities that he built in Hamath.
And he built the upper Beis Horon and the lower Beis Horon, fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars.

And Baalath and all the store cities that Shlomo had and all the cities for his chariots and the cities for his horsemen, and all Shlomo's desire, which he desired to build in Yerushalayim and in Levanon and in all the land of his realm.
All the people remaining from the Chitim, the Emorim, the Perizzim, the Chivim, and the Yevusim, who were not of Yisroel.
Of their children who remained after them in the land, whom the Children of Yisroel had not annihilated-Shlomo subjected them to forced labor until this day.
But of the Children of Yisroel, Shlomo did not make into slaves for his work, because they were men of war and the officers over his commanders and the officers of his chariots and his horsemen.
And these are the officers over King Shlomo's appointed men-two hundred fifty, who ruled over the people.

And Paroh's daughter Shlomo brought up from the City of Dovid to the house that he had built for her, because he said: No wife of mine shall dwell in the house of Dovid, king of Yisroel, because they [the places] are holy, since the Ark of Havayah came into them.
Then Shlomo offered up burnt offerings to Havayah on the altar of Havayah, which he had built before the vestibule.

And as the duty of every day required, to offer up according to the commandment of Moshe; for the Sabbaths, for the New Moons, and for the appointed seasons three times a year; on the Feast of Unleavened Bread, on the Feast of Weeks, and on the Feast of Tabernacles.

And he stationed, according to the ordinance of his father Dovid, the divisions of the priests on their service and the Leviim on their watches, to praise and to serve opposite the priests, for the daily requirement on its day, and the gate sentries in their divisions for every gate, for so was the command of Dovid the man of Elokim.
And they did not deviate [from] the king's command to the priests and the Leviim regarding every matter and for the treasuries.
And all Shlomo's work was established until this day, [from] the founding of the House of Havayah until its completion, when the House of Havayah was complete.
Then Shlomo went to Etzion-Geber and to Eilot on the seashore in the land of Edom.

And Huram sent him through his servants ships and servants who had knowledge of the sea, and they came with Shlomo's servants to Ofir, and they took from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold and brought it to King Shlomo.

And the queen of Sheva heard of Shlomo's fame, and she came to test Shlomo with riddles in Yerushalayim with an exceedingly large retinue, with camels bearing spices and gold in abundance and precious stones; and she came to Shlomo and spoke with him all that was in her heart.
And Shlomo answered all her questions, and nothing was hidden from Shlomo that he did not tell her.
And the queen of Sheva saw Shlomo's wisdom and the House that he had built.

And the food of his table and the seating of his servants and the station of his attendants and their attire and his cupbearers and their attire, and his ascent by which he would go up to the Temple of Havayah, and she was breathless.
And she said to the king, "It was a true report that I heard in my country of your deeds and of your wisdom.
But I did not believe their words until I came and saw with my own eyes, and behold, not half of your abundant wisdom was told me; you have [wisdom] in excess of the report that I heard.
Fortunate are your men, and fortunate are these your servants who always stand before you and listen to your wisdom.

Blessed be Havayah your Elokim, Who desired you, to place you on His throne to be king for Havayah your Elokim because of your Elokim's love for Yisroel to establish them forever, and He appointed you as king over them to do justice and righteousness."
And she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold and very abundant spices and precious stones; there were never such spices as those that the queen of Sheva gave to King Shlomo.
And also, Huram's servants and Shlomo's servants, who brought gold from Ofir, brought algom wood and precious stones.
And Shlomo made of the algom wood a path to the House of Havayah and to the king's palace, and harps and psalteries for the singers; none like them had been seen before in the land of Yehudah.
And King Shlomo gave the queen of Sheva all her wish that she requested, aside from that which she brought to the king, and she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.
And the weight of gold that came to Shlomo in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold.
Aside from that which the guides and the merchants would bring, and all the kings of Arabia and the regents of the land brought gold and silver to Shlomo.
And King Shlomo made two hundred shields of malleable gold; six hundred malleable gold pieces would go into one shield.
And three hundred shields of malleable gold; three hundred gold pieces would go into one shield, and Shlomo placed them in the house of the forest of Levanon.
And the king made an immense ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.
And there were six steps to the throne, and the throne had a ramp of gold attached to the throne, with armrests on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
And twelve lions were standing there on the six steps on either side; the like was not made for any kingdom.
And all King Shlomo's drinking vessels were gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Levanon were of superior gold; silver was not reckoned as anything in Shlomo's time.
For the king had ships going to Tarshish with Huram's servants; once in three years ships of Tarshish would come, bearing gold and silver, ivory and apes and peacocks.
Now King Shlomo transcended all the kings of the Earth in affluence and in wisdom.
And all the kings of the Earth sought Shlomo's presence to hear the wisdom with which Elokim had endowed him.
And each one would bring his gift, vessels of silver and vessels of gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules, the tribute due each year in its year.
And Shlomo had four thousand stables of horses and chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Yerushalayim.
And he ruled over all the kings, from the River until the land of the Pelishtim and until the border of Mitzrayim.
And the king made silver as common in Yerushalayim as stones, and cedars he made as common as sycamores that are in the lowlands in abundance.
And they brought horses for Shlomo from Mitzrayim and from all the lands.

And the rest of Shlomo's deeds, the first and the last, are they not written in the words of Nasan the prophet and in the prophecy of Achiyah the Shiloni, and in the visions of Yedo the seer concerning Yeravam the son of Nebat.
And Shlomo reigned in Yerushalayim over all Yisroel forty years.
And Shlomo slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Dovid his father, and Rechavam his son reigned in his place.
And Rechavam went to Shechem, for all Yisroel had come to Shechem to make him king.
And it was when Yeravam the son of Nebat heard of this, and he was in Mitzrayim where he had fled from the presence of King Shlomo, that Yeravam returned from Mitzrayim.
And they sent and called him, and Yeravam came, and all Yisroel, and they spoke to Rechavam, saying:
"Your father made our yoke hard, and now, lighten your father's hard work and his heavy yoke that he placed upon us, and we shall serve you."
And he said to them, "Another three days, and return to me," and the people departed.
And King Rechavam conferred with the elders who had stood before Shlomo his father when he was alive, saying, "How do you advise to reply to this people?"
And they spoke to him saying, "If you will be kind to this people, and you will appease them and speak to them good words, they will be your servants for all times."
But he disregarded the counsel of the elders, which they advised him, and he conferred with the youths who had grown up with him, who were standing before him.
And he said to them, "What do you advise that we reply to this people, who spoke to me, saying: Lighten the yoke that your father placed upon us?"

And the youths who had grown up with him spoke to him saying, "So shall you say to the people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, and you lighten it from upon us'; so shall you say to them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
And now, where my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I shall add to your yoke. My father flogged you with whips, but I [shall do so] with scorpions.'
And Yeravam and all the people came to Rechavam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
And the king answered them harshly, and King Rechavam disregarded the counsel of the elders.
And he spoke to them according to the counsel of the youths, saying, "[My father] made your yoke heavy, and I shall add to it; my father flogged you with whips, but I [shall do so] with scorpions."
And the king did not heed the people because it was brought about by Elokim, so that Havayah might establish His word that He spoke by the hand of Achiyah the Shiloni to Yeravam the son of Nebat.

And all Yisroel [saw] that the king had not heeded them, and the people replied to the king, saying, "What share do we have in Dovid? And no heritage in Yishai's son. Each man, to your homes, O Yisroel! Now see your house, Dovid!" And all Yisroel went to their homes.
But the Children of Yisroel who dwelt in the cities of Yehudah-Rechavam reigned over them.

And King Rechavam sent Hadoram, who was appointed over the tax, and the Children of Yisroel pelted him with stones and he died, and King Rechavam exerted himself to get up into his chariot to flee to Yerushalayim.
And the Yisroelim rebelled against the house of Dovid until this day.

And Rechavam came to Yerushalayim, and he assembled the house of Yehudah and Binyamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to wage war with the House of Yisroel, to restore the kingdom to Rechavam.
And the word of Havayah came to Shemayah, the man of Elokim, saying:
"Speak to Rechavam, the son of Shlomo, king of Yehudah, and to all Yisroel in Yehudah and Binyamin, saying:

So Havayah said, 'You shall not go up and you shall not war with your brothers; return each man to his home for this thing has been brought about by Me."' And they heeded the word of Havayah, and they returned from going to Yeravam.
And Rechavam dwelt in Yerushalayim, and he built cities for fortification in Yehudah.
And he built Beis Lechem and Etam and Tekoa.
And Beis-Zur and Socho and Adulam.
And Gat and Maresha and Zif.
And Adoraim and Lachish and Azekah.
And Zoreah and Ayalon and Chevron, which are in Yehudah and in Binyamin, fortified cities.
And he strengthened the fortifications, and he placed in them leaders, and storehouses of food, oil, and wine.
And in every city [he placed] shields and spears, and he made them exceedingly strong, and Yehudah and Binyamin were his.
And the priests and the Leviim who were in all Yisroel stood by him in all their boundary.

For the Leviim had abandoned their open land and their heritage, and they went to Yehudah and to Yerushalayim, because Yeravam and his sons had coerced them to abandon their position of ministering to Havayah.
And he stationed for himself priests for the high places and for the satyrs, and for the calves that he had made.
And after them, from all the tribes of Yisroel, those who put their heart to seek Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, came to Yerushalayim to sacrifice to Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers.
And they strengthened the kingdom of Yehudah and supported Rechavam the son of Shlomo for three years, for they went in the way of Dovid and Shlomo for three years.
And Rechavam took himself a wife, Mahalath the daughter of Yerimos the son of Dovid, [and] Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Yishai.
And she bore him sons: Jeush and Shemaryah and Zaham.
And after her he took Maacah the daughter of Avshalom, and she bore him Aviyah and Attai and Ziza and Shelomis.
And Rechavam loved Maacah the daughter of Avshalom more than all his wives and his concubines, for he married eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he begot twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
And Rechavam appointed Aviyah the son of Maacah to be the head, as a leader among his brothers, in order to make him king.
And he understood, and he dispersed of all his sons to all the lands of Yehudah and Binyamin, to all the fortified cities, and he gave them abundant food, and he sought many wives.
Now it came to pass when Rechavam's kingdom was established and when he became strong, he abandoned the Law of Havayah, and all Yisroel with him.
And it came to pass in the fifth year of King Rechavam, that Shishak the king of Mitzrayim marched against Yerushalayim, for they had betrayed Havayah.
With a thousand and two hundred chariots and with sixty thousand horsemen, and there was no number to the people who came with him from Mitzrayim: the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Kushim.
And he seized Yehudah's fortified cities, and he came until Yerushalayim.

And Shemayah the prophet came to Rechavam and the princes of Yehudah who had gathered to Yerushalayim because of Shishak, and he said to them, "So Havayah said: You have forsaken Me; so I too have forsaken you in the hand of Shishak."
And the princes of Yisroel and the king humbled themselves, and they said, "Havayah is just."

And when Havayah saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of Havayah came to Shemayah, saying, "They have humbled themselves; I shall not destroy them, but I shall grant them some measure of deliverance, and My wrath will not be poured out in Yerushalayim by the hand of Shishak.
For they will be his slaves, and they will know My service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands.

And Shishak, the king of Mitzrayim, marched against Yerushalayim, and he took the treasures of the House of Havayah and the treasures of the king's palace; everything he took, and he took the golden shields that Shlomo had made.
And King Rechavam made instead of them copper shields, and he entrusted them in the hands of the chiefs of the runners, who guarded the entrance of the king's palace.
And it came to pass that whenever the king came to the House of Havayah, the runners came and carried them and returned them to the chamber of the runners.
And when he humbled himself, Havayah's wrath returned from him, and [He did] not [say] to destroy [him] completely, and also in Yehudah were good things.

And King Rechavam strengthened himself in Yerushalayim and reigned, for Rechavam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and seventeen years he reigned in Yerushalayim — the city that Havayah had chosen wherein to place His name, out of all the tribes of Yisroel; and his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonis.
And he did that which was evil, for he did not set his heart to seek Havayah.

And the deeds of Rechavam, the first and the last, are they not written in the words of Shemayah the prophet and Iddo the seer in the manner of genealogy, and the wars of Rechavam and Yeravam all the times.
And Rechavam slept with his forefathers, and he was buried in the City of Dovid, and Aviyah his son reigned in his stead.
In the eighteenth year of King Yeravam, Aviyah began to reign over Yehudah.
Three years he reigned in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Michayah the daughter of Uriel from Givah, and there was a war between Aviyah and Yeravam.
And Aviyah conducted the war with an army of mighty warriors, four hundred thousand chosen men, and Yeravam waged war with him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty warriors.
And Aviyah arose at the top of Mount Zemaraim, which is on Mount Efrayim, and he said, "Hearken to me, Yeravam and all Yisroel.
Should you not know that Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, gave the kingdom to Dovid over Yisroel forever, to him and to his sons, [with] a covenant of salt?
But Yeravam the son of Nebat, the servant of Shlomo the son of Dovid, arose and rebelled against his master.
And there gathered to him worthless and unbridled men, and they overwhelmed Rechavam the son of Shlomo, and Rechavam was young and soft-hearted, and he did not strengthen himself before them.

And now, you are saying to strengthen yourselves before the kingdom of Havayah in the hand of the sons of Dovid, and you are a great multitude, and with you are golden calves that Yeravam made for you for gods.

Did you not banish the priests of Havayah, the sons of Aharon, and the Leviim, and make for yourselves priests like the peoples of the lands? Whoever comes to initiate himself with a young bull and seven rams, will be a priest to a non-god.
But, as for us — Havayah is our Elokim, and we have not forsaken Him, and the priests who minister to Havayah are the sons of Aharon, and the Leviim engage in the work.

And they burn to Havayah burnt offerings every morning and every evening, and incense and [set up] the showbread on the pure table, and the golden candelabrum and its lamps to kindle every evening, for we keep the watch of Havayah our Elokim, but you have forsaken Him.

And behold, with us at the head are Elokim and His priests and the sounding trumpets to sound over you. O Children of Yisroel, do not wage war with Havayah, the Elokim of your forefathers, for you will not succeed."
And Yeravam turned the ambush to come from behind them, and they were before Yehudah, and the ambush was behind them.
And Yehudah turned around, and behold the battle was before them and behind them, and they cried out to Havayah, and the priests were sounding the trumpets.
And the men of Yehudah shouted, and it came to pass, when the men of Yehudah shouted, Elokim smote Yeravam and all Yisroel before Aviyah and Yehudah.
And the Children of Yisroel fled before Yehudah, and Elokim delivered them into their hands.
And Aviyah and his people smote them a great blow, and five hundred thousand chosen men of Yisroel fell slain.
And the Children of Yisroel were humbled at that time, and the Children of Yehudah became strong because they relied on Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers.
And Aviyah pursued Yeravam, and he captured cities from him; Beis-El and its villages and Yeshanah and its villages and Efrain and its villages.
And Yeravam could muster no more strength in the days of Aviyah, and Havayah smote him, and he died.
And Aviyah strengthened himself, and he took himself fourteen wives, and he begot twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
And the rest of the deeds of Aviyah and his ways and his deeds are written in the midrash of the prophet Iddo.
And Aviyah slept with his forefathers, and they buried him in the City of Dovid, and his son Asa reigned in his stead; in his time, the land was tranquil for ten years.
Now Asa did what was good and proper in the eyes of Havayah his Elokim.
And he removed the foreign altars and the high places, and he shattered the monuments and cut down the asherim.
And he commanded Yehudah to seek Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers and to perform the Law and the commandments.
And he removed from all the cities of Yehudah the high places and the sun images, and the kingdom was tranquil before him.
And he built fortified cities in Yehudah, because the land was tranquil, and there was no war with him in these years, because Havayah gave him peace.

And he said to Yehudah, "Let us build these cities and encompass them with a wall and towers and doors and bars as long as the land is before us, for we sought Havayah our Elokim; we sought [Him] and He gave us peace from round about." So they built and prospered.
And Asa had an army bearing shields and spears, from Yehudah three hundred thousand and from Binyamin bearing shields and drawing the bow, two hundred eighty thousand, all these mighty warriors.
And Zerah the Kushi came out against them with an army of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah.
And Asa came out before him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephath at Mareshah.

And Asa called out to Havayah his Elokim, and he said, "O Havayah, there is no difference to You to help either the great or the powerless; help us, O Havayah our Elokim, for we have relied on You, and we have come with Your name upon this multitude. You are Havayah our Elokim; let no man rule against You.
And Havayah smote the Kushim before Asa and before Yehudah, and the Kushim fled.

And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them all the way to Gerar, and there fell from the Kushim until they had no life, for they were broken before Havayah and before His camp, and they carried away very much spoils.
And they smote all the cities around Gerar, because the fear of Havayah was upon them, and they plundered all the cities because there was much plunder in them.
And they also smote the tents of the livestock, and they captured many sheep and camels, and they returned to Yerushalayim.
And the spirit of Elokim was upon Azaryah the son of Oded.

And he went out before Asa and said to him, "Hearken to me, Asa and all of Yehudah and Binyamin; Havayah is with you because you are with Him, and if you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
Now there were many days for Yisroel without a true Elokim and without an instructing priest, and without the Torah.
And they returned to Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, when they were in distress, and they sought Him, and He was found by them.
And in those times, there was no peace for anyone going or coming for there were great turmoils upon all the inhabitants of the lands.
And nation was crushed by nation and city by city, because Elokim discomfited them with all troubles.
But you be strong and let your hands not slacken, for there is reward for your work."

And when Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he strengthened himself and removed the abominations from all the land of Yehudah and Binyamin and from the cities that he had captured from Mount Efrayim, and he renewed the altar of Havayah, which was in front of the vestibule of Havayah.

And he gathered all Yehudah and Binyamin and those dwelling with them from Efrayim and Menasheh and from Shimon, for many of Yisroel had defected to them when they saw that Havayah their Elokim was with them.
And they gathered to Yerushalayim in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
And they sacrificed to Havayah on that day of the plunder [that] they brought; cattle, seven hundred, and sheep, seven thousand.
And they entered the covenant to seek Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers, with all their heart and with all their soul.
And whoever would not seek Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, shall be put to death, from the smallest to the greatest, whether man or woman.
And they swore to Havayah with a loud voice and with shouting, and with trumpets and with shopharoth.
And all Yehudah rejoiced over the oath, because they had sworn with all their heart, and they sought Him with all their will, and He was found by them, and Havayah gave them rest from round about.
And also Maacah, King Asa's mother, he deposed from [being] the queen because she had made a frightful image for an asherah, and Asa cut off her image, crushed it and burnt it in Kidron Valley.
The high places, however, were not removed from Yisroel, but Asa's heart was perfect all his days.
And he brought the hallowed objects of his father and his own hallowed objects to the House of Elokim-silver, gold, and vessels.
And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's kingdom, Baasha, the king of Yisroel, advanced on Yehudah, and he built the Ramah, so as not to allow anyone either to leave or enter to Asa, king of Yehudah.
And Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the House of Havayah and the house of the king, and he sent to Ben Hadad, the king of Aram, who dwelt in Damesek, saying:

"There is a treaty between me and you and between my father and your father; behold I have sent you silver and gold. Go, abrogate your treaty with Baasha, the king of Yisroel, that he may depart from me."
And Ben Hadad heeded King Asa, and he sent the officers of his army to the cities of Yisroel, and they smote Ijjon and Dan and Avel-Mayim, and all the storehouses of the cities of Naftali.
Now it came to pass when Baasha heard, that he stopped building the Ramah and he discontinued his work.
And King Asa took all of Yehudah and they carried away the stones of the Ramah and its wood, which Baasha had built, and with them he built Geva and Mitzpah.

And at that time Chanani the seer came to Asa, king of Yehudah, and he said to him, "When you relied on the king of Aram, and you did not rely on Havayah your Elokim; therefore, the army of the king of Aram escaped from your hand.
Were not the Kushim and the Lubim a huge host with very many chariots and horsemen? But when you relied on Havayah, He delivered them into your hand.

For Havayah-His eyes run to and fro throughout the entire earth to grant strength with those whose heart is whole toward Him. You have dealt foolishly in this matter, for from now on you shall have wars.
And Asa was incensed against the seer, and he put him into the prison-house, for he was wroth with him about this, and Asa crushed some of the people at that time.
And behold the deeds of Asa, the first and the last, behold they are written in the book of the kings of Yehudah and Yisroel.
And Asa suffered from a foot ailment in the thirty-ninth year of his reign until his ailment spread upward, and also in his illness, he did not seek Havayah, but the physicians.
And Asa slept with his forefathers, and he died in the forty-first year of his reign.

And they buried him in his graves that he had dug for himself in the City of Dovid, and they laid him on a couch that he had filled with spices and diverse kinds [of spices], prepared with the perfumer's art, and they kindled an exceedingly great fire for him.
And Yehoshafat his son reigned in his stead, and he strengthened himself over Yisroel.
And he stationed an army in all the fortified cities of Yehudah, and he stationed garrisons in the land of Yehudah and in the cities of Efrayim, which Asa his father had seized.
And Havayah was with Yehoshafat because he went in the first ways of Dovid his father, and did not inquire of the baalim.
But he inquired of the Elokim of his father, and he went in His commandments, and not like Yisroel's deeds.
And Havayah established the kingdom in his hand, and all Yehudah gave a gift to Yehoshafat, and he had abundant riches and glory.
And his heart was uplifted in the ways of Havayah, and he further removed the high places and the asherim from Yehudah.
And in the third year of his reign, he sent his officers, Ben Hail, Ovadyah, Zecharyah, Nethanel, and Michayah, to teach in the cities of Yehudah.
And with them were the Leviim: Shemayah, Nesanyah, Zevadyah, Asahel, Shemiramos, Yehonasan, Adoniyah, Toviyah, and Tob Adoniyah, the Leviim, and with them were Elishama and Yehoram, the priests.
And they taught in Yehudah, and with them was the scroll of the Law of Havayah and they went around throughout all the cities of Yehudah, and they taught among the people.
And the fear of Havayah was upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Yehudah, and they did not wage war with Yehoshafat.
And some of the Pelishtim brought Yehoshafat gifts and loads of silver; also the Arvim brought him flocks; rams-seven thousand and seven hundred, and goats-seven thousand and seven hundred.
And Yehoshafat was becoming greater to an unusual degree, and he built in Yehudah towers and store cities.
And he had much work in the cities of Yehudah, and men of war, mighty warriors, in Yerushalayim.
And this was their number according to the house of their fathers: of Yehudah the officers over the thousands were Adnah the chief, and with him, mighty warriors-three hundred thousand.
And beside him was Yehochanan the chief, and with him two hundred eighty thousand.
And beside him was Amatzyah the son of Zichri, who gave generously to Havayah, and with him were two hundred thousand mighty warriors.
And from Binyamin was a mighty warrior, Eljada, and with him, armed with bow and shield, were two hundred thousand.
And beside him was Yehozavad and with him one hundred and eighty thousand advance guards.
These were the ministers of the king, in addition to those whom the king had stationed in the fortified cities throughout all Yehudah.
Now Yehoshafat had abundant riches and honor, and he allied himself in marriage with Ahab.

And he went down at the end of [several] years to Ahab, to Shomron, and Ahab slaughtered for him abundant sheep and cattle, and for the people who were with him, and he enticed him to go up to Ramos-Gilad.

And Ahab, the king of Yisroel, said to Yehoshafat, the king of Yehudah, "Will you go with me to Ramos-Gilad?" And he said to him, "Like me like you, and like your people are my people, and [they will go up] with you in battle."
And Yehoshafat said to the king of Yisroel, "Please inquire today the word of Havayah."

And the king of Yisroel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and he said to them, "Shall we go to Ramos Gilad, or shall I refrain?" and they said, "Ascend, and Elokim will deliver [it] into the hands of the king."
And Yehoshafat said, "Is there no other prophet of Havayah here from whom we may inquire?"

And the king of Yisroel said to Yehoshafat, "There is one more man from whom to inquire the word of Havayah, but I hate him for he does not prophesy good about me, but always bad; he is Michayah the son of Imla." And Yehoshafat said, "The king should not say that."
And the king of Yisroel summoned one eunuch, and said, "Bring Michayah the son of Imla at once."

Now the king of Yisroel and Yehoshafat, king of Yehudah, were seated each on his throne, dressed in [their] attire and seated in a threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomron, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
And Tzidkiyah the son of Chenaanah made himself iron horns, and he said, "So Havayah said: With these you shall gore Aram until you destroy them completely."
And all the prophets were prophesying likewise, saying, "Go up to Ramos-Gilad and triumph, and Havayah will deliver [it] into the king's hand."

And the messenger who had gone to summon Michayah spoke to him, saying, "Behold, the words of the prophets are unanimously favorable to the king. Now let your word be like one of theirs, and you shall speak favorably."
And Michayah said, "As Havayah lives, whatever my Elokim will say, that I will speak."
And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Michah, shall we go to Ramos-Gilad to war or shall I refrain?" And he said, "Go up and triumph, and may they be delivered into your hand."
And the king said to him, "How many times must I adjure you, that you shall not speak to me but truth in the name of Havayah?"
And he said, "I saw all the Yisroelim scattered over the mountains like sheep who have no shepherd. And Havayah said: These have no master. Let them return each one to his house in peace."
And the king of Yisroel said to Yehoshafat, "Did I not say to you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, only bad?"
And he said, "Therefore, listen to the word of Havayah. I saw Havayah seated on His throne, and all the host of heaven were standing on His right and His left.
And Havayah said: Who will entice Ahab, king of Yisroel so that he will go up and fall in Ramos-Gilad? One said thus, and another said thus.
And a certain spirit came forth and stood before Havayah and said: I will entice him. And Havayah said to him: Wherewith?
And he said: I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And He said: You will entice and you will prevail. Go forth and do so.
And now, behold Havayah has placed a lying spirit in the mouth of these, your prophets, but Havayah has spoken evil concerning you."
And Tzidkiyah the son of Chenaanah approached and struck Michayah on the cheek, and said, "Which way did the spirit of Havayah pass from me to speak with you?"
And Michayah said, "Behold you will see on that day that you will come into a chamber within a chamber to hide."
And the king of Yisroel said, "Take Michayah and return him to Amon the mayor of the city and to Yoash the king's son.
And you shall say: So the king said: Place this person in prison and feed him a scant amount of bread and a scant amount of water until I return in peace."
And Michayah said, "If you return in peace, Havayah did not speak to me." And he said, "All ye peoples, listen."
And the king of Yisroel and Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah went up to Ramos-Gilad.
And the king of Yisroel said to Yehoshafat, "[I will] disguise myself and go into battle, but you may wear your [royal] garb; so the king of Yisroel disguised himself, and they went into battle.
And the king of Aram commanded the officers of his chariots, saying, "Attack neither small nor great, except only the king of Yisroel."

And it was when the officers of the chariots saw Yehoshafat that they said, "That is the king of Yisroel." They turned upon him to attack [him], and Yehoshafat cried out, and Havayah helped him, and Elokim enticed them away from him.
And it was when the officers of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Yisroel, that they turned back from [going] after him.

And a man drew his bow innocently and it hit the king of Yisroel between the scales and the coat of mail, and he said to the charioteer, "Turn your hand and carry me out of the camp for I have become sick."
And the battle withdrew on that day, and the king of Yisroel was standing in the chariot against the Aramim until evening, and he died at the time of the setting of the sun.
And Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah returned home in peace to Yerushalayim.

And Yehu the son of Chanani, the seer, came out before him, and said to King Yehoshafat, "[Did you go] to aid the wicked, and do you love those who hate Havayah? Now because of this there is wrath upon you from before Havayah.
Nevertheless there are good things found in you, for you have abolished the asheroth from the land, and you set your heart to seek Elokim."
And Yehoshafat dwelt in Yerushalayim, and he returned and went forth among the people from Be'er Sheva to Mount Efrayim, and he brought them back to Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers.
And he appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Yehudah, for every city.
And he said to the judges, "See what you are doing, for you do not judge for man but for Havayah, and [He] is with you in the matter of the judgment.
And now, may the fear of Havayah be upon you; observe and do, for with Havayah your Elokim there is neither injustice, favoritism, nor bribe-taking."

And also in Yerushalayim, Yehoshafat set up judges of the Leviim and the priests and of the chiefs of the fathers' [houses] of Yisroel, for the judgment of Havayah and for quarrels, and they returned to Yerushalayim.
And he commanded them, saying, "So shall you do in fear of Havayah, in faith, and with a perfect heart.

And whenever any quarrel comes to you from your brethren who dwell in their cities, between blood[shed] and blood[shed], between instruction of the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances, you shall admonish them, so that they should not be guilty before Havayah, and there be wrath upon you and upon your brethren; so shall you do, and you will not be guilty.

And behold, Amaryah the head priest is over you for every matter of Havayah, and Zevadyah the son of Yishmael is the leader of the house of Yehudah for every matter of the king, and the Levi law-enforcers are before you; be strong and do, and may Havayah be with the good."
And it came to pass afterwards that the children of Moav and the children of Ammon, and with them some of the Ammonim, came to Yehoshafat to [wage] war.
And they came and told Yehoshafat, saying, "A great multitude has come upon you from across the sea, from Aram, and behold they are in Hazazon-Tamar; the same is Ein-Gedi."
And Yehoshafat was frightened and set his face to seek Havayah, and he proclaimed a fast over all Yehudah.
And the Yehudim gathered to seek help of Havayah; also from all the cities of Yehudah they came to seek Havayah.
And Yehoshafat stood in the assembly of Yehudah and Yerushalayim in the House of Havayah, before the new court.

And he said, "O Havayah, Elokim of our fathers, is it not so that You are Elokim in heaven, and that You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations, and in Your hand is strength and might, and no one can stand with You?
Have you, our Elokim, not driven out the inhabitants of this land from before Your people Yisroel and given it to the seed of Avraham, who loved You, forever?
And they dwelt therein and therein they built You a Sanctuary for Your name, saying:

Should evil come upon us, whether sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine, we shall stand before this House and before You, for Your name is in this House, and we shall cry out to You from our distress, and You will hear and save.

And now, behold the children of Ammon and Moav and Mount Seir, against whom You did not permit Yisroel to come when they came out of the land of Mitzrayim, for they turned away from them and did not destroy them.
And behold they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of Your inheritance, which You caused us to inherit.
Our Elokim, will You not execute judgment upon them? For we have no strength before this great multitude that is coming upon us, and we know not what to do, but our eyes are upon You."
And all the Yehudim stood before Havayah, also their infants, their wives, and their children.
And Yahaziel the son of Zecharyah the son of Benayahu the son of Yeiel the son of Matanyah the Levi of the sons of Asaf — the spirit of Havayah was upon him in the midst of the assembly.

And he said, "Hearken, all Yehudim, inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and King Yehoshafat, so Havayah said to you: You shall not fear, neither shall you be dismayed because of this great multitude, for the war is not yours but Elokim's.
Tomorrow, descend upon them; behold they are ascending on the ascent to Haziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, before the desert of Yeruel.

It is not for you to fight in this [war]; set yourselves, stand and see the salvation of Havayah with you, O Yehudah and Yerushalayim; fear not and be not dismayed. Tomorrow, go forth before them, and Havayah will be with you."
And Yehoshafat bowed upon his face to the ground, and all the Yehudim and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim fell before Havayah to prostrate themselves to Havayah.
And the Leviim of the sons of the Kehasim and of the sons of the Korchim arose to praise Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, with an exceedingly loud voice.

And they arose early in the morning and went forth to the desert of Tekoa, and when they went forth, Yehoshafat stood and said, "Hear me, O Yehudim and inhabitants of Yerushalayim. Believe in Havayah your Elokim, and you will be believed; believe in His prophets, and you will prosper."

And he took counsel with the people, and he set up singers to Havayah that they should praise the beauty of holiness, when they went out before the advance guard and said, "Give thanks to Havayah, for His kindness is eternal."
And at the time they commenced with song and praise, Havayah placed liers-in-wait against the children of Ammon, Moav, and Mount Seir, who were coming to Yehudah, and they were struck down.
And the children of Ammon and Moav rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to destroy and annihilate, and when they finished with the inhabitants of Seir, each one helped his friend to destroy.
And the Yehudim came upon the place overlooking the desert, and they turned to the multitude, and behold they were corpses falling to the ground, with no survivors.

And Yehoshafat and his people came to plunder the spoils, and they found among them plenty, and belongings and corpses and precious vessels, which they emptied out for themselves to the extent that they could not carry them away, and for three days they were plundering the spoil, because it was so much.
And on the fourth day, they congregated to the valley of Berachah, for there they blessed Havayah; therefore, they named that place the valley of Berachah to this day.
And all the men of Yehudah and Yerushalayim returned with Yehoshafat at their head, to return to Yerushalayim with joy, because Havayah had given them joy [by saving them] from their enemies.
And they came to Yerushalayim with psalteries, with harps, and with trumpets to the House of Havayah.
And fright of Elokim was upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that Havayah had fought with Yisroel's enemies.
And Yehoshafat's kingdom was tranquil, and Elokim granted him peace from round about.
And Yehoshafat reigned over Yehudah; he was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
And he went in the way of his father Asa and did not turn away from it, to do what was right in the eyes of Havayah.
But the high places were not removed, and the people had not yet set their hearts to the Elokim of their forefathers.
And the rest of the affairs of Yehoshafat — the first ones and the last ones-behold they are written in the words of Yehu the son of Chanani, which was inserted in the book of the kings of Yisroel.
And afterwards, Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah joined Achazyah the king of Yisroel, who dealt wickedly.
And he joined himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made ships in Etzion-Geber.
And Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied about Yehoshafat, saying, "When you joined Achazyah, Havayah breached your work." And the ships were broken and could not go to Tarshish.
And Yehoshafat slept with his forefathers and was buried with his forefathers in the City of Dovid, and Yehoram his son reigned in his stead.
And he had brothers, the sons of Yehoshafat; Azaryah, Yechiel, Zecharyah, Azariahu, Michoel, and Shefatyah; all these were the sons of Yehoshafat the king of Yisroel.
And their father gave them many gifts of silver, of gold, and of precious things, with fortified cities in Yehudah, but the kingdom he gave to Yehoram, because he was the firstborn.
And Yehoram rose upon the kingdom of his father, and he strengthened himself and assassinated all his brothers with the sword, and also of the chieftains of Yisroel.
Yehoram was thirty two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim.
And he went in the ways of the kings of Yisroel, as the house of Ahab did, for a daughter of Ahab became his wife, and he did that which was evil in Havayah's eyes.
Now Havayah was unwilling to destroy the house of Dovid because of the covenant that He had made with Dovid, and as He said to give him a kingdom and to his sons for all times.
In his days, Edom rebelled from under the power of Yehudah, and they appointed a king over themselves.
And Yehoram crossed with his chieftains and all the chariots with him, and he arose at night, and he smote the Edomim who surrounded him, and the chiefs of the chariots.
And Edom rebelled from under the power of Yehudah until this day; then Libnah rebelled at that time from under his power because he had forsaken Havayah, the Elokim of his forefathers.
He too made high places in the mountains of Yehudah, and led the inhabitants of Yerushalayim astray, and led Yehudah astray.

And a letter came to him from Eliyahu the prophet, saying, "So Havayah said, the Elokim of Dovid your father: Because you did not go in the ways of Yehoshafat your father and in the ways of Asa, the king of Yehudah.

And you went in the way of the kings of Yisroel, and you led Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim astray, as the house of Ahab led astray, and also you assassinated your brothers of your father's house, who were better than you.
Behold Havayah will smite your people with a great plague, and your sons and your wives and all your possessions.
And you will have many illnesses with the illness of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the illness, days upon days."
And Havayah stirred up against Yehoram the spirit of the Pelishtim and the Arvim, who dwell alongside the Kushim.

And they marched upon Yehudah and split it, and they captured all the possessions found belonging to the king's house, and also his sons and his wives, and no son was left to him except Yehoachaz, the youngest of his sons.
And after all this, Havayah plagued him in his bowels with an incurable illness.

And it was that in the passing of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out by reason of his illness, and he died with malignant illnesses, and his people did not make for him a burning like the burning of his forefathers.

He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Yerushalayim for eight years, and he departed joyless, and they buried him in the City of Dovid, but not in the graves of the kings.

And the inhabitants of Yerushalayim made Achazyah his youngest son king in his stead, for the troop that had come from the Arvim to the camp had slain all the first ones, and Achazyah, the son of Yehoram the king of Yehudah reigned.
Achazyah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Atalyah the daughter of Omri.
He too went in the ways of the house of Ahab, because his mother would advise him to deal wickedly.
And he did that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah as did the house of Ahab, because they were his advisors after his father's death, to bring about his destruction.
He, too, followed their counsel, and he went with Yehoram the son of Ahab, the king of Yisroel, to war against Hazael, the king of Aram in Ramos-Gilad, and the Aramim smote Yoram.

And he went back to be healed in Yizreel because of the smiters who smote him in Ramah, when he waged war with Hazael the king of Aram, and Azaryah the son of Yehoram king of Yehudah went down to see Yehoram the son of Ahab in Yizreel because he was ill.

Now the downfall of Achazyah was from Elokim, insofar as he came to Yoram, and when he came, he went out with Yehoram to Yehu the son of Nimshi, whom Havayah had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it came to pass when Yehu executed justice upon the house of Ahab, that he found the chiefs of Yehudah and the sons of Achazyah's brothers, ministering to Achazyah, and he slew them.

And he sought Achazyah and they seized him, and he was hiding in Shomron, and they brought him to Yehu, and they slew him, and they buried him, for they said, "He is the son of Yehoshafat, who sought Havayah with all his heart," and the house of Achazyah could not muster up strength for the kingdom.
And [when] Atalyah the mother of Achazyah, saw that her son was dead, she rose and destroyed all those of royal descent of the house of Yehudah.

And Yehoshavas, the king's daughter took Yoash the son of Achazyah and stole him away from among the slain children of the king, and she placed him and his nurse in the bed-chamber, and Yehoshavas the daughter of King Yehoram, the wife of Yehoyada the priest, concealed him-because she was the sister of Achazyah - from before Atalyah, and she did not slay him.
And he hid with them in the House of Elokim for six years, and Atalyah reigned over the land.

And in the seventh year, Yehoyada gained strength, and he took the chiefs of the hundreds, Azaryah the son of Yerocham, Yishmael the son of Yehochanan, Azaryah the son of Obed, Maaseyah the son of Adayah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, with him in a covenant.
And they went about in Yehudah and gathered the Leviim from all the cities of Yehudah, and the chiefs of the fathers' [houses] of Yisroel, and they came to Yerushalayim.
And the entire congregation enacted a covenant in the House of Elokim with the king, and he said to them, "Behold the king's son shall reign, as Havayah spoke concerning the sons of Dovid.
This is the thing that you shall do: a third of you, of those coming in on the Sabbath, of the priests and of the Leviim, shall be gatekeepers of the thresholds.
And a third shall be in the king's palace, and a third in the Yesod gate, and all the people in the courts of the House of Havayah.
And no one shall enter the House of Havayah, except the priests and the ministers of the Leviim; they shall enter, because they are holy, and all the people shall keep Havayah's watch.

And the Leviim shall surround the king, each one with his weapons in his hand, and whoever enters the House shall be put to death, and you shall be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."

And the Leviim and all Yehudah did according to all that Yehoyada the priest commanded, and they took each one his men, of those coming in on the Sabbath with those leaving on the Sabbath, for Yehoyada the priest did not dismiss the divisions.
And Yehoyada gave to the chiefs of the hundreds the spears, the bucklers, and the shields of King Dovid, which were in the House of Elokim.
And he stationed the entire people, and each one with his sword in his hand, from the right side of the House to the left side of the House, before the altar and the House, surrounding the king.
And they brought out the king's son and placed upon him the crown and the testimony, and they made him king, and Yehoyada and his sons anointed him and said, "Long live the king!"
And Atalyah heard the sound of the people, running and praising the king, and she came to the people, to the House of Havayah.

And she saw, and behold, the king was standing on his stand in the entrance, and the officers and the trumpets beside the king, and the people of the land rejoicing and sounding the trumpets, and the singer [played] on musical instruments and led the singing of praise, and Atalyah rent her garments and said, "Treason! Treason!"

And Yehoyada the priest brought out the officers of the hundreds, those appointed over the army, and said to them, "Take her out to within the ranks, and whoever follows her is to be put to death by the sword, for the priest said, "Do not put her to death in the House of Havayah."
And they made a place for her, and she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate to the king's palace, and they put her to death there.
And Yehoyada enacted a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should become Havayah's people.
And all the people came to the temple of the Baal and tore it down, and its alters and its images they smashed, and Mattan the priest of the Baal they slew before the altars.

And the priest set up appointees over the House of Havayah in the hand of the priests the Leviim, whom Dovid had divided over the House of Havayah to offer up the burnt offerings of Havayah, as is written in the Law of Moshe, with joy and with song, by the hands of Dovid.
And he stationed the gate keepers over the gates of the House of Havayah, so that no one who was unclean should enter for any matter.

And he took the officers of the hundreds and the mighty men and the rulers over the people and all the people of the land, and he brought the king down from the House of Havayah, and they came within the upper gate to the king's palace, and they sat the king upon the throne of the kingdom.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, and they slew Atalyah by the sword.
Yoash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Tzivyah from Be'er Sheva.
And Yoash did what was proper in the eyes of Havayah all the days of Yehoyada the priest.
And Yehoyada took himself two wives, and he begot sons and daughters.
And it came to pass afterwards that it was in Yoash's heart to renew the House of Havayah.

And he gathered the priests and the Leviim and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Yehudah and gather money from all Yisroel to strengthen the House of your Elokim from year to year, and you hasten to the matter," but the Leviim did not hasten.

So the king summoned Yehoyada the chief and said to him, "Why did you not demand of the Leviim to bring from Yehudah and from Yerushalayim the tax of Moshe the servant of Havayah, and the congregation of Yisroel, for the Tent of the Testimony?"
For the wicked Atalyah — her sons had breached the House of Elokim, and also, all the hallowed things of the House of Havayah they had made for the baalim.
And the king ordered, and they made one chest, and they placed it in the gate of the House of Havayah, to the outside.
And they announced in Yehudah and in Yerushalayim to bring to Havayah the tax of Moshe the servant of Elokim upon Yisroel in the desert.
And all the officers and all the people rejoiced, and they brought and cast into the chest until they were finished.

Now it came to pass at the time that the chest was brought to the appointment of the king by the hand of the Leviim, and when they saw that there was much money, the king's scribe and the appointee of the head priest would come, empty the chest, carry it and return it to its place. So they did day by day, and they gathered money in abundance.

And the king and Yehoyada gave it to the foremen of the work of the service of the House of Havayah, and hired [stone]cutters and craftsmen to renew the House of Havayah, and also for craftsmen of iron and copper to strengthen the House of Havayah.
The workmen did their work, and the work was improved by them, and they set up the House of Elokim on its base, and they strengthened it.

And when they finished, they brought before the king and Yehoyada the rest of the money, and he made it into vessels for the House of Havayah, service vessels, and pestles and spoons and gold and silver vessels, and they would constantly offer up burnt offerings in the House of Havayah, all the days of Yehoyada.
