Now Yehoyada grew old and was sated with days, and he died; he was a hundred and thirty years old upon his death.
And they buried him in the City of Dovid with the kings, for he had done good in Yisroel and with Elokim and His house.
And after the death of Yehoyada, the princes of Yehudah came and prostrated themselves to the king; then the king hearkened to them.
And they forsook the House of Havayah, the Elokim of their fathers, and they worshiped the asherim and the idols, and there was wrath upon Yehudah and Yerushalayim because of this, their guilt.
And He sent prophets among them, to return them to Havayah, and they warned them, but they did not incline their ears.

And the spirit of Elokim enveloped Zecharyah the son of Yehoyada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, "So Elokim said: Why do you transgress the commandments of Havayah? You will not succeed because you have forsaken Havayah, and He has forsaken you."
And they conspired against him and stoned him by the king's command, in the forecourt of the House of Havayah.
And King Yoash did not remember the loving-kindness that Yehoyada his father had done with him, but he killed his son, and upon his death he said, "May Havayah see and requite."

And it came to pass at the turn of the year that the army of Aram marched upon him, and they came to Yehudah and Yerushalayim, and they destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people, and all their plunder they sent to the king of Damesek.

For, with few men the army of Aram came, and Havayah delivered into their hands an exceedingly large army, for they had forsaken Havayah, the Elokim of their fathers; and they dealt out punishment to Yoash.

And when they went away from him, for they left him with many ailments, his servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Yehoyada the priest, and they slew him on his bed, and he died, and they buried him in the City of Dovid, but they did not bury him in the graves of the kings.
And these were the ones who conspired against him: Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonis, and Yehozavad the son of Shimrith the Moavis.

And concerning his sons, and the many prophecies about him, and the foundation of the House of Elokim-behold they are inscribed in the midrash of the book of the kings; and Amatzyah his son reigned in his stead.
When he was twenty-five years old, Amatzyah became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. His mother's name was Yehoadan of Yerushalayim.
He did what was right in the eyes of Havayah, but not wholeheartedly.
And it was when the kingdom became well established with him, that he executed his servants who had assassinated the king his father.

But their sons he did not execute, for as is written in the Torah, in the book of Moshe, that Havayah had commanded, saying: "Fathers shall not die for sons, nor shall sons die for fathers, but each man shall die for his own sin."

And Amatzyah gathered Yehudah and stood them up according to their fathers' houses, according to the chiefs of the thousands and the chiefs of the hundreds for all Yehudah and Binyamin, and he counted them from twenty years and upward, and he found them three hundred thousand youths who go out to the army, who hold a spear and a shield.
And he hired of Yisroel one hundred thousand mighty warriors for a hundred talents of silver.
And a man of Elokim came to him, saying, "O king, let not the army of Yisroel come with you, for Havayah is not with Yisroel, even with all the sons of Efrayim.
But if you come, do, strengthen yourself for war, [lest] Elokim cause you to stumble before the enemy, for Elokim has strength to help or to cause to stumble."

And Amatzyah said to the man of Elokim, "But what shall I do about the hundred talents that I gave to the Yisroeli troop?" And the man of Elokim replied, "Havayah has much more than this to give you."
And Amatzyah separated the troop that had come to him from Efrayim to go to their place, and they were very angry with Yehudah, and they returned to their place in fierce anger.
And Amatzyah strengthened himself and led his people, and he went to the Valley of Salt, and he smote the children of Seir, ten thousand.
And the children of Yehudah captured ten thousand alive, and they brought them to the top of the rock, and they cast them from the top of the rock, and they were all split open.

And the members of the troop that Amatzyah had sent back that they should not go with him to war, raided the cities of Yehudah from Shomron to Beis-Horon, and they smote three thousand of them and plundered much booty.

And it was, after Amatzyah had come from smiting the Edomim, that he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up for himself for gods, and he prostrated himself before them and burned incense to them.
And Havayah became wroth with Amatzyah, and He sent him a prophet, and he said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of the people who did not save their people from your hand?"

And it was when he spoke to him, that he replied to him, "Did we make you an adviser to the king? Desist. Why should they smite you?" So the prophet desisted, and he said, "I know that Elokim has given counsel to destroy you, because you have done this, and you have not heeded my counsel."
And Amatzyah, the king of Yehudah, took counsel, and he sent to Yoash the son of Yehoachaz the son of Yehu, the king of Yisroel, saying, "Come, let us confront each other."

And Yoash the king of Yisroel sent to Amatzyah the king of Yehudah, saying, "The thistle that was in Levanon sent to the cedar that was in Levanon, saying: Give your daughter to my son for a wife; and the wild beast that was in Levanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
You said that behold, you have defeated Edom, and your heart has made you haughty to seek glory. Now, stay in your home. Why should you provoke evil and fall, you and Yehudah with you?"
But Amatzyah did not heed, because this was from Elokim, in order to deliver them into their hands, for they had sought the gods of Edom.
And Yoash the king of Yisroel went up, and they confronted one another, he and Amatzyah the king of Yehudah, in Beis-Shemesh, which belongs to Yehudah.
And Yehudah was beaten before Yisroel, and they fled each man to his tent.

And Yoash the king of Yisroel seized Amatzyah the king of Yehudah, the son of Yoash the son of Yehoachaz, in Beis Shemesh, and he brought him to Yerushalayim and breached the wall of Yerushalayim from the Gate of Efrayim until the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

And [he took] all the gold and silver and all the vessels that were found in the House of Elokim with Obed-Edom, and the treasures of the king's palace, and the hostage children; and he returned to Shomron.
And Amatzyah the son of Yoash the king of Yehudah lived fifteen years after the death of Yoash the son of Yehoachaz the king of Yisroel.
And the rest of the deeds of Amatzyah, both the earlier ones and the later ones — are they not written in the book of the kings of Yehudah and Yisroel?
And from the time that Amatzyah turned away from following Havayah, they conspired against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Lachish. And they sent after him to Lachish and assassinated him there.
And they carried him on the horses, and they buried him with his forefathers in the city of Yehudah.
And the entire people of Yehudah took Uziyah, who was sixteen years old, and they made him king instead of his father Amatzyah.
He built Eilot and restored it to Yehudah, after the king slept with his forefathers.
Uziyah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Yecholyah of Yerushalayim.
And he did what was right in the eyes of Havayah, as all that Amatzyah his father had done.
And [it was his custom] to seek Elokim in the days of Zecharyah, who understood the visions of Elokim, and when he sought Havayah, Elokim caused him to prosper.
And he went forth and waged war with the Pelishtim, and he breached the wall of Gat and the wall of Yavneh and the wall of Ashdod, and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Pelishtim.
And Elokim helped him against the Pelishtim and against the Arvim who dwelt in Gur-Baal and the Meunim.
And the Ammonim gave Uziyah a gift, and his name went until the approach to Mitzrayim, for he had become exceedingly strong.
And Uziyah built towers in Yerushalayim at the Corner Gate and at the Valley Gate and at the corner, and he strengthened them.

And he built towers in the desert, and he hewed many cisterns, for he had much cattle and in the lowlands and in the plains, plowmen and vinedressers in the mountains and in the fruitful fields, for he loved the soil.

And Uziyah had a force of warriors who went out to war by bands, according to the number of their counting, by the hand of Yeiel the scribe and Maaseyah the officer, under the hand of Chananyah, one of the king's chiefs.
The entire number of the heads of the fathers' [houses], of the mighty warriors-two thousand and six hundred.
And under their jurisdiction, an army of three hundred thousand and seven thousand and five hundred, those who wage war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
And Uziyah prepared for them, for the entire host, shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and sling stones.

And he made in Yerushalayim engines, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and on the corners, to shoot with arrows and with huge stones, and his name went forth far abroad for he did wondrous things to help himself, until he became strong.

And when he became strong, his heart became haughty until he became corrupt, and he trespassed against Havayah his Elokim, and he came into the Temple of Havayah to burn incense on the altar of incense.
And Azaryah the priest came after him, and with him were priests of Havayah, eighty mighty men.

And they stood beside Uziyah the king and said to him, "It is not for you, Uziyah, to burn incense to Havayah, but for the priests, sons of Aharon, who are consecrated to burn [incense]. Leave the Sanctuary, for you have trespassed, and it will not be glory for you from Havayah Elokim."

And Uziyah became furious, and in his hand was a censer to burn, and in his fury with the priests, the zaraath shone upon his forehead before the priests in the House of Havayah, over the altar of incense.

And Azaryah, the chief priest, and all the priests, turned to him, and behold he was stricken with zaraath on his forehead; so they rushed him out of there, and he too hastened to leave, for Havayah had smitten him.

And King Uziyah was stricken with zaraath until the day of his death, and he lived in a house of retirement, for it had been decreed from the House of Havayah, and Yosam his son was over the king's house; he judged the people of the land.
And the rest of the events of Uziyah, both the earlier ones and the later ones, Yeshayah the son of Amoz the prophet inscribed.
And Uziyah slept with his forefathers, and they buried him with his forefathers in the cemetery of the kings, for they said, "He is a mezora," and Yosam his son reigned in his stead.
Yosam was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Yerushah the daughter of Tzadok.
He did what was proper in the eyes of Havayah, as all that his father Uziyah had done; only he did not enter the Temple of Havayah; but the people were still acting corruptly.
He built the upper gate of the House of Havayah, and in the wall of the rampart he built extensively.
And he built cities in Mount Yehudah, and in the forests he built palaces and towers.

And he fought with the king of the children of Ammon, and he overpowered them, and the children of Ammon gave him in that year a hundred talents of silver and ten thousand kor of wheat and ten thousand of barley; this the children of Ammon returned to him, and in the second year and the third.
And Yosam became powerful, because he prepared his ways before Havayah his Elokim.
And the rest of the affairs of Yosam and all his wars and his ways-behold they are inscribed in the book of the kings of Yisroel and Yehudah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim.
And Yosam slept with his forefathers, and they buried him in the City of Dovid, and his son Achaz reigned in his stead.
Achaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned for sixteen years in Yerushalayim, and he did not do that which was proper in the eyes of Havayah like his father Dovid.
And he went in the ways of the kings of Yisroel, and he also made molten images for the baalim.
And he burnt incense in the valley of Ben Hinnom, and he burnt his sons in fire, like the abominations of the nations whom Havayah had driven out from before the Children of Yisroel.
And he sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places and on the hills and under every leafy tree.

And Havayah his Elokim delivered him into the hand of the king of Aram, and they smote him and captured from him a great captivity, and they brought them to Damesek, and he was also delivered into the hand of the king of Yisroel, and he smote him a great blow.
And Pekah the son of Remalyah slew in Yehudah one hundred and twenty thousand in one day, all of whom were valiant men, when they forsook Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers.
And Zichri, a mighty man of Efrayim, slew Maaseyah, the king's son, and Azrikam, the ruler of the palace, and Elkanah, the viceroy.

And the Children of Yisroel captured of their brethren two hundred thousand women, male children, and female children, and they also took a large amount of spoils from them, and they brought the spoils to Shomron.

Now there was a prophet of Havayah there named Oded, and he went out before the army coming to Shomron, and he said to them, "Behold because of the wrath of Havayah, the Elokim of your forefathers upon Yehudah, He delivered them into your hand, and you slew them with fury that reached the heavens.
And now, the children of Yehudah and Yerushalayim you say to hold for manservants and maidservants for yourselves. Are you not bringing with yourselves only guilt against Havayah Elokim?
And now, hearken to me and return the captives whom you have captured from your brethren, for the burning wrath of Havayah is upon you."

And certain men of the chiefs of the sons of Efrayim: Azaryah the son of Yehochanan, Berechyah the son of Meshillemoth and Yechizkiyah the son of Shalum and Amassa the son of Hadlai, stood up against those coming from the army.

And they said to them, "Do not bring the captives here, for what to Havayah is guilt upon us you intend to add to our sins and to our guilt, for this will be great guilt to us and burning wrath upon Yisroel."
And the advance guard left the captives and the booty before the officers and all the assembly.

And the men who were mentioned by name arose and took hold of the captives, and clothed all their nakedness from the spoils, and they dressed them and shod them and fed them and gave them to drink, and they anointed them and led them on donkeys, every feeble one, and they brought them to Yericho, the city of palms, beside their brethren, and they returned to Shomron.
At that time, King Achaz sent to the kings of Ashur to aid him.
Also Edomim came, and they slew of Yehudah and captured captives.

And Pelishtim raided the cities of the lowlands and the southland of Yehudah, and they captured Beis Shemesh and Ayalon and Gederoth and Socho and its villages and Timnah and its villages, and Gimzo and its villages and they dwelt there.
For Havayah had humbled Yehudah because of Achaz, king of Yisroel, for he exposed Yehudah and acted treacherously against Havayah.
And Tillegath-Pilneser, the king of Ashur, came upon him and oppressed him but did not strengthen him.
For Achaz had shared [the treasures of] the House of Havayah and the palace of the king and the princes, and he gave them to the king of Ashur, but he was of no help to him.
And at the time he oppressed him, he continued to act treacherously against Havayah; he was King Achaz.

And he sacrificed to the gods of the kings of Aram, who had smitten him, and he said, "For the gods of the kings of Aram — they are helping them. To them I shall sacrifice, and they will help me," but they caused him to stumble, as well as all Yisroel.

And Achaz gathered the vessels of the House of Elokim, and he cut the vessels of the House of Elokim, and he closed the doors of the House of Havayah, and he made himself altars in every corner in Yerushalayim.
And in every city of Yehudah he made high places to burn incense to strange gods; and he angered Havayah, the Elokim of his forefathers.
And the rest of his affairs and all his ways, both the earlier ones and the later ones-behold they are inscribed in the book of the kings of Yehudah and Yisroel.
And Achaz slept with his forefathers, and they buried him in the city, in Yerushalayim, but they did not bring him to the graves of the kings of Yisroel, and Chizkiyah his son reigned in his stead.
Chizkiyah became king at the age of twenty-five years, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Aviyah the daughter of Zecharyah.
And he did that which was proper in the eyes of Havayah, as all that his father Dovid had done.
He, in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the House of Havayah and reinforced them.
And he brought the priests and the Leviim and gathered them into the eastern square.
And he said to them, "Hear me, ye Leviim; now sanctify yourselves and sanctify the House of Havayah, the Elokim of your fathers, and remove the 'menstruant' from the Sanctuary.
For our fathers acted treacherously and did evil in the eyes of Havayah, our Elokim and forsook Him, and they turned their faces away from the Tabernacle of Havayah and turned their backs.
Moreover, they closed the doors of the vestibule, and extinguished the lamps, and they did not burn incense nor offer up burnt offerings in the Sanctuary to the Elokim of Yisroel.
And the anger of Havayah was against Yehudah and Yerushalayim, and He made them for a shudder, an astonishment, and a hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
And behold, our fathers have fallen by the sword and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity because of this.
Now it is with my heart to make a covenant with Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, so that His burning wrath should turn from us.
My sons, now do not forget, for Havayah chose you to stand before Him to minister to Him and to be His ministers and to burn incense."

Then there arose the Leviim: Mahath the son of Amasai and Yoel the son of Azaryah of the sons of the Kehasim, and of the sons of Merari: Kish the son of Abdi and Azaryah the son of Yehalelel, and of the Gershonim, Yoah the son of Zimmah and Eden the son of Yoah.
And of the sons of Elitzafan: Shimri and Yeiel, and of the sons of Asaf: Zecharyah and Matanyah.
And of the sons of Heiman: Yechiel and Shimi, and of the sons of Yedusun: Shemayah and Uzziel.
And they assembled their brethren and sanctified themselves, and they came according to the commandment of the king concerning the matters of Havayah, to purify the House of Havayah.

And the priests came within the House of Havayah to purify [it], and they took out all the uncleanness that they found in the Temple of Havayah to the court of the House of Havayah, and the Leviim received it to take it out to the Kidron Valley outside.

They commenced on the first of the first month to sanctify, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the vestibule of Havayah; and they sanctified the House of Havayah for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month, they finished.
And they came within to King Chizkiyah, and they said, "We have purified the entire House of Havayah and the burnt-offering altar and all its vessels, and the table of showbread and all its vessels.
And all the vessels that King Achaz forsook during his reign, with his treachery — we have prepared and sanctified, and here they are before the altar of Havayah."
And King Chizkiyah arose early and gathered the officers of the city and went up to the House of Havayah.

And they brought seven bulls and seven rams and seven lambs and seven kids for sin-offerings for the kingdom and for the Sanctuary and for Yehudah, and he said to the sons of Aharon, the priests, to offer them up on the altar of Havayah.

And they slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood, and they sprinkled it upon the altar, and they slaughtered the rams and sprinkled the blood upon the altar, and they slaughtered the lambs and sprinkled the blood upon the altar.
And they brought the kids for sin-offerings before the king and the congregation, and they placed their hands upon them.
And the priests slaughtered them and sprinkled their blood upon the altar to atone for all Yisroel, because for all Yisroel the king said [to offer] the burnt-offerings and the sin-offerings.

And he stationed the Leviim in the House of Havayah, with cymbals, with psalteries, and with harps, by the commandment of Dovid and Gad the king's seer and Nasan the prophet, for by the hand of Havayah was the commandment, by the hand of His prophets.
And the Leviim stood with Dovid's instruments, and the priests with the trumpets.

And Chizkiyah said to bring up the burnt-offerings to the altar, and at the time that the burnt-offering commenced, the song of Havayah and the trumpets commenced and by means of the instruments of Dovid, king of Yisroel.
And the entire congregation prostrated themselves, and the song was sung, and the trumpets were sounded; everything [continued] until the completion of the burnt-offerings.
And when they finished offering them up, the king and all those found with him kneeled and prostrated themselves.
And King Chizkiyah and the officer ordered the Leviim to praise Havayah with the words of Dovid and Asaf the seer, and they praised until they were joyful, and they bowed and prostrated themselves.

And Chizkiyah answered and said, "Now you have invested yourselves to Havayah; come close and bring [peace-] offerings and thanksgiving offerings to the House of Havayah," and the congregation brought [peace-]offerings and thanksgiving-offerings, and every generous-hearted one - burnt offerings.
And the number of burnt-offerings that the congregation brought was: seventy oxen, a hundred rams, two hundred lambs; all these were burnt-offerings to Havayah.
And the sacred offerings were six hundred large cattle and three thousand small cattle.

Only the priests were few, and they could not flay all the burnt-offerings; so their brethren, the Leviim, reinforced them until the work was completed and until the priests consecrated themselves, for the Leviim were more conscientious than the priests to consecrate themselves.
And also, there were many burnt-offerings with the fats of the peace-offerings and with the libations for the burnt-offerings, and the service of the House of Havayah was established.
And Chizkiyah and all the people rejoiced over that which Elokim had prepared for the people, because the matter was sudden.

And Chizkiyah sent to all Yisroel and Yehudah, and he also wrote letters to Efrayim and Menasheh to come to the House of Havayah in Yerushalayim, to perform the Passover sacrifice to Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel.
And the king and his officers and the entire congregation took counsel in Yerushalayim, to perform the Passover sacrifice in the second month.
For they could not perform it at that time, for the priests had not consecrated themselves sufficiently, and the people had not gathered to Yerushalayim.
And the matter was proper in the eyes of the king and in the eyes of the entire congregation.

And they issued a statement to announce throughout all Yisroel, from Be'er Sheva to Dan to come to perform a Passover sacrifice to Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, in Yerushalayim, because for many years they had not performed it as it is written.

So the couriers went with the letters from the hand of the king and his officers throughout all Yisroel and Yehudah, and according to the king's command, saying, "Children of Yisroel, return to Havayah, the Elokim of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yisroel, so that He may return to the remnant that has escaped from the clutches of the kings of Ashur.
And do not be like your fathers or like your brothers, who acted treacherously against Havayah, the Elokim of their fathers, and He made them a desolation, as you see.

Now, do not be stiffnecked like your fathers; give a hand to Havayah and come to His Sanctuary which He consecrated forever, and worship Havayah your Elokim, so that His burning wrath returns from you.

For when you return to Havayah, your brothers and your sons will find compassion before their captors and shall return to this land, for Havayah your Elokim is gracious and merciful, and He will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him."
Now the couriers passed from city to city in the land of Efrayim and Menasheh, even to Zevulun, and they laughed at them and mocked them.
But people from Asher and Menasheh and from Zevulun humbled themselves and came to Yerushalayim.
The hand of Elokim was also upon Yehudah to give them one accord, to perform the command of the king and the officers concerning the word of Havayah.
And a huge crowd assembled in Yerushalayim to observe the Festival of Matzoth in the second month, an exceedingly large assembly.
And they arose and removed the altars that were in Yerushalayim, and all the altars for incense they removed and cast them into the Kidron Valley.

And they slaughtered the Passover sacrifice on the fourteenth day of the second month, and the priests and the Leviim were embarrassed, and they consecrated themselves and brought burnt-offerings to the House of Havayah.
And they stood in their station as was their custom, according to the Torah of Moshe, the man of Elokim; the priests sprinkled the blood from the hand of the Leviim.

For there were many among the congregation who had not consecrated themselves, and the Leviim were in charge of the slaughter of the Passover sacrifices for everyone who was unclean, to make it holy for Havayah.

For a multitude of the people, many from Efrayim and Menasheh, Yissachar and Zevulun, had not purified themselves, for they ate the Passover sacrifice not as it is written, for Chizkiyah had prayed for them, saying, "May the good Havayah atone for
Anyone who has set his whole heart to seek Elokim, Havayah, the Elokim of his forefathers, though [he be] not [cleaned] according to the purity that pertains the holy things."
And Havayah hearkened to Chizkiyah and healed the people.

And the Children of Yisroel who were present in Yerushalayim observed the Festival of Matzoth for seven days with great joy, the Leviim and the priests praised Havayah day by day, with powerful instruments to Havayah.

And Chizkiyah prevailed upon all the Leviim who were experts in the service of Havayah, and they ate [the sacrifices of] the appointed season for seven days, sacrificing peace-offerings and thanking Havayah, the Elokim of their forefathers.
And the entire congregation took counsel to keep another seven days; and they kept seven days of joy.

For Chizkiyah, the king of Yehudah, separated for the congregation one thousand bulls and seven thousand small cattle, and the officers separated for the congregation one thousand bulls and ten thousand small cattle, and the priests consecrated themselves in great numbers.

And the entire congregation of Yehudah and the priests and the Leviim and the entire congregation that came from Yisroel, and the strangers that came from the land of Yisroel, and those who dwelt in Yehudah, rejoiced.
And there was great joy in Yerushalayim, for since the days of Shlomo the son of Dovid, king of Yisroel [there had] not [been] the like in Yerushalayim.
And the priests, the Leviim, arose and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to His holy habitation, to heaven.

And when they completed all this, all the Yisroelim who were present went out to the cities of Yehudah, and they smashed the monuments and cut down the asherim, and they demolished the high places and the altars from all Yehudah and Binyamin and in Efrayim and Menasheh until they had completely destroyed [them], and all the Children of Yisroel returned, each man to his inheritance, to their cities.

And Chizkiyah stationed the divisions of the priests and the Leviim in their divisions each man according to his service, for the priests and for the Leviim; for burnt-offerings and for peace-offerings, to minister and to thank and praise in the gates of the camps of Havayah.

And the king's portion from his possessions for the burnt-offerings, for the burnt-offerings of the morning and the evening and the burnt-offerings for the Sabbaths and for the New Moons and for the appointed seasons, as is written in the Law of Havayah.
And he commanded the inhabitants of Yerushalayim to give the portion of the priests and the Leviim, in order that they be strengthened in the Law of Havayah.
And when the word burst forth, the Children of Yisroel increased the first of corn, wine, oil, honey, and all the increase of the field, and the tithes of everything they brought in abundance.

And the Children of Yisroel and Yehudah who lived in the cities of Yehudah — they too brought tithes of large cattle and small cattle and the tithes of sacred things consecrated to Havayah their Elokim, and they gave many stacks.
In the third month, they commenced to lay the foundations of the stacks, and in the seventh month they finished.
And Chizkiyah and his officers came, and they saw the stacks, and they blessed Havayah and His people Yisroel.
And Chizkiyah demanded of the priests and the Leviim concerning the stacks.

And Azaryah, the chief priest of the house of Tzadok, said to him, and he said, "From the beginning of bringing the heave-offering to the House of Havayah, we ate to satiety and left over in abundance, for Havayah had blessed His people, and what is left over is this abundance."
And Chizkiyah ordered to prepare the chambers in the House of Havayah, and they prepared [them].
And they brought the heave-offerings and the tithes and the sacred things faithfully, and over them was the ruler, Conanyah the Levi, and Shimi his brother, the second in command.

And Yechiel and Azazyah and Nahath and Asahel and Yerimos and Yozabad and Eliel and Yismachyah and Mahath and Benayahu, appointees under the jurisdiction of Conanyah and Shimi his brother, by the command of King Chizkiyah and Azaryah the ruler of the House of Elokim.
And Kore the son of Imnah the Levi, the gate sentry of the East Gate was over the donations of Elokim, to give the heave-offering of Havayah and the most holy of the sacred things.

And next to him were Eden and Minjamin and Yeshua and Shemayah, Amaryah and Shechanyah in the cities of the priests in offices of trust, to give their brethren in the divisions, to the great as to the small.

Besides those who traced their genealogy, of the males from three years old and upwards, for everyone who comes to the House of Havayah, for his daily necessities, for their service in their watches, according to their divisions.
And the priests who traced their genealogy to the house of their fathers, and the Leviim from twenty years old and upwards, in their watches, in their divisions.
And for all those whose genealogy was traced, concerning all their infants, their wives, and their sons and daughters, of every congregation, for with their faith they consecrated the holy things.

And for the sons of Aharon the priests, in the fields of the open land of their cities, in every city, were men who were mentioned by names, to give portions to every male among the priests and to all who traced their lineage among the Leviim.
And Chizkiyah did accordingly in all the cities of Yehudah, and he did what was good and proper and true before Havayah his Elokim.
And in every deed that he commenced in the service of the House of Elokim and in the Law and in the commandment, to seek Elokim; he did with all his heart and prospered.
After these deeds of integrity, Sennacherib the king of Ashur came, and he entered into Yehudah and encamped against the fortified cities, and he planned to make a breach therein for himself.
And Chizkiyah saw that Sennacherib had come, and his face was directed to wage war against Yerushalayim.
And he took counsel with his officers and his mighty men to stop up the waters of the fountains that were outside the city, and they assisted him.
And a large multitude gathered and stopped up all the fountains and the stream that flowed in the midst of the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Ashur come and find much water?"

And he strengthened himself and built the whole breached wall, and he raised it to the towers and outward to the other wall, and he reinforced the millo, the City of Dovid, and he made many swords and shields.
And he appointed officers of war over the people, and he gathered them to him to the square of the gate of the city, and he spoke encouragingly to them, saying:

"Be strong and of good courage; do not fear and do not be dismayed because of the king of Ashur and because of all the multitude that is with him, because He Who is with us is greater than those with him.
With him is an arm of flesh, and with us is Havayah our Elokim to help us and to wage our wars," and the people relied on the words of Chizkiyah, king of Yehudah.

After this, Sennacherib the king of Ashur sent his servants to Yerushalayim — and he was besieging Lachish, and all his staff was with him-to Chizkiyah the king of Yehudah, and to all the Yehudim who were in Yerushalayim, saying:
"So Sennacherib said the king of Ashur: In what do you trust that you stay in the siege in Yerushalayim?
Is not Chizkiyah enticing you to give you over to die by famine and thirst, saying: Havayah, our Elokim, will save us from the clutches of the king of Ashur?
Did not he - Chizkiyah - remove His high places and His altars and say to Yehudah and to Yerushalayim, saying: Before one altar you shall prostrate yourselves, and upon it you shall burn incense?
Do you not know what I did-I and my forefathers-to all the peoples of the lands? Could the gods of the nations of the lands save their land from my hand?
Who is it among all the gods of these nations whom my fathers destroyed, that could save his people from my hand, that your Elokim should be able to save you from my hand?

And now, let Chizkiyah not deceive you, and let him not entice you like this, and do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom could save his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers; surely your Elokim will not save you from my hand."
And his servants spoke further against Havayah Elokim and against Chizkiyah His servant.

And he wrote letters to blaspheme Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel, and to say about Him, saying, "Like the gods of the nations of the lands, which did not save their people from my hand, so will the Elokim of Chizkiyah not save His people from my hand."
And they called out with a loud voice in Yehudi to the people of Yerushalayim who were on the wall, to frighten them and to terrify them, so that they might seize the city.
And they spoke of the Elokim of Yerushalayim as of the gods of the peoples of the land, the handiwork of man.
And King Chizkiyah and the prophet, Yeshayah the son of Amoz prayed concerning this, and they cried out to Heaven.

And Havayah sent an angel, and he destroyed every mighty warrior and ruler and officer in the camp of the king of Ashur, and he returned shamefacedly to his land, and he entered the temple of his god, and some of his own issue felled him there with the sword.
And Havayah saved Chizkiyah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim from the hand of Sennacherib the king of Ashur and from the hand of all, and He led them from roundabout.
And many brought an offering to Havayah to Yerushalayim and delicacies to Chizkiyah the king of Yehudah, and he was elevated in the eyes of all the nations henceforth.
In those days, Chizkiyah became ill until he was near death, and he prayed to Havayah, and he spoke to him, and he gave him a sign.
But Chizkiyah did not repay Him according to that which He had bestowed upon him, for his heart became haughty, and there was wrath upon him and upon Yehudah and Yerushalayim.
And Chizkiyah became humbled when his heart was haughty, he and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and the wrath of Havayah did not come upon them in the days of Chizkiyah.
And Chizkiyah had much wealth and honor, and he made himself treasuries for silver, for gold, for precious stones, for spices, for shields, and for all precious vessels.
And storehouses for the increase of corn, wine, and oil, and stalls for all kinds of beasts, and flocks for sheepfolds.
And he made himself cities and possessions of small cattle and large cattle in abundance, for Elokim gave him exceedingly abundant possessions.
And he-Chizkiyah-stopped up the source of the waters of the upper Gichon, and he led them straight down on the west to the City of Dovid, and Chizkiyah prospered in all his works.
And so, because of the emissaries of the officers of Bavel, who sent to him to seek the sign that was in the land, Elokim forsook him to test him to know all that was in his heart.
And the rest of the affairs of Chizkiyah and his kind acts-behold they are written in the vision of Yeshayah the son of Amoz the prophet, in the book of the kings of Yehudah and Yisroel.

And Chizkiyah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the best of the sepulchres of the sons of Dovid, and all of Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim bestowed honor upon him at his death, and Menasheh his son reigned in his stead.
Menasheh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yerushalayim fifty-five years.
And he did that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah, like the abominations of the nations that Havayah had driven out from before the Children of Yisroel.

And he rebuilt the high places that his father Chizkiyah had demolished, and he erected altars to the baalim, and he made asheroth, and he prostrated himself to the entire host of the heaven, and he worshipped them.
And he built altars in the House of Havayah, concerning which Havayah had said, "In Yerushalayim, My name shall be forever."
And he built altars to the entire host of heaven in the two courts of the House of Havayah.

And he passed his sons through fire in the valley of Ben Hinnom; he practiced soothsaying, divination, and sorcery, and he consulted necromancers and those who divine by the jidoa bone; he did much that was evil in the eyes of Havayah, to provoke Him.

And he placed the graven image of the idol that he made, in the House of Elokim, concerning which Elokim had said to Dovid and to his son Shlomo, "In this House and in Yerushalayim, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Yisroel, I will establish My name forever.

And I will not continue to remove Yisroel's feet from the land that I have given their forefathers; if they will but observe to do all that I have commanded them, and according to all the Law, the statutes, and the ordinances that Moshe My servant commanded them."
And Menasheh led Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim astray to do what was evil, more than the nations whom Havayah had destroyed from before the Children of Yisroel.
And Havayah spoke to Menasheh and to his people, but they did not listen.
And Havayah brought upon them the generals of the king of Ashur, and they seized Menasheh with hooks and bound him with copper chains and brought him to Bavel.
And when he was distressed, he entreated Havayah his Elokim, and he humbled himself greatly before the Elokim of his fathers.
And he prayed to Him, and He accepted his prayer, and He heard his supplication and He restored him to Yerushalayim to his kingdom, and Menasheh knew that Havayah was Elokim.

And afterwards, he built an outer wall to the City of Dovid on the west of Gichon in the valley, even to the Fish Gate, and he surrounded the Ofel and raised it exceedingly, and he placed military officers in all the fortified cities in Yehudah.

And he removed the foreign gods and the idol from the House of Havayah and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the House of Havayah and in Yerushalayim, and he cast them outside the city.
And he built the altar of Havayah, and he sacrificed on it peace-offerings and thanksgiving offerings, and he told Yehudah to worship Havayah Elokim of Yisroel.
But the people were still sacrificing on the high places, but only to Havayah their Elokim.

And the rest of Menasheh's affairs and his prayer to his Elokim, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel-behold they are with the affairs of the kings of Yisroel.

And his prayer and its acceptance, and his sin and his treacherous acts, and the places where he built high places and erected the asherim and the graven images before he humbled himself-behold they are inscribed with the words of Hozai.
And Menasheh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his house, and Amon his son reigned in his stead.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Yerushalayim.
And he did that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah as Menasheh his father had done, and to all the graven images that Menasheh his father had made, Amon sacrificed, and he worshipped them.
And he did not humble himself before Havayah as Menasheh his father had done, for he-Amon-became more and more guilty.
And his servants conspired against him and assassinated him in his palace.
And the people of the land slew all the conspirators against King Amon, and the people of the land made Yoshiyah his son king in his stead.
Yoshiyah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yerushalayim thirty-one years.
And he did that which was right in the eyes of Havayah, and he walked in the ways of Dovid his father, and turned aside neither to the right nor to the left.

And in the eighth year when he became king, when he was still a youth, he started to seek after the Elokim of Dovid his father, and in the twelfth year he started to purge Yehudah and Yerushalayim of the high places, the asherim, the graven images, and the molten images.

And they demolished before him the altars of the baalim and the sun images that were above them he cut down, and the asherim, the graven images, and the molten images he smashed and crushed, and he cast them upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
And the bones of the priests he burned on their altars, and he purged Yehudah and Yerushalayim.
And in the cities of Menasheh and Efrayim and Shimon as far as Naftali with their instruments of destruction round about.
And he demolished the altars, and the asherim and the graven images he crushed into dust, and all the sun images he cut down in all the land of Yisroel, and he returned to Yerushalayim.

And in the eighteenth year of his reign, after the purging of the land and the Temple, he sent Shafan the son of Atzalyah and Maaseyah, the ruler of the city, and Yoah the son of Yoahaz the recorder to strengthen the House of Havayah his Elokim.

And they came to Chilkiyah the High Priest and gave the silver that was brought to the House of Elokim, which the Leviim who guarded the threshold had gathered from the hands of Menasheh and Efrayim and from all the remnant of Yisroel and from all Yehudah and Binyamin, and they returned to Yerushalayim.

They gave it into the hands of the foremen of the work, who were appointed in the House of Havayah, and they gave it [to] the workers who were working in the House of Havayah, to mend and repair the House.
And they gave it to the carpenters and to the builders to buy hewn stones and wood for the couplings, and to make beams for the houses that the kings of Yehudah had destroyed.

And the men did the work faithfully, and over them were appointed Yahath and Ovadyah the Leviim of the sons of Merari, and Zecharyah and Meshullam of the sons of the Kehasim to direct, and the Leviim, all who were expert with musical instruments.
And over the porters and the overseers over all those who did the work, for every work, and of the Leviim, scribes and officers and gate sentries.
And when they took out the silver that was brought into the House of Havayah, Chilkiyah the priest found the Scroll of the Law of Havayah by the hand of Moshe.
And Chilkiyah spoke up and said to Shafan the scribe, "I have found the Scroll of the Law in the House of Havayah," and Chilkiyah gave the scroll to Shafan.
And Shafan brought the scroll to the king, and he further brought back word to the king, saying, "Whatever was given into the hands of your servants they are doing."
And they poured the silver that was found in the House of Havayah, and they gave it into the hands of those appointed and into the hands of those who did the work.
And Shafan the scribe told the king, saying, "Chilkiyah the priest gave me a scroll," and Shafan read from it before the king.
And it was when the king heard the words of the Law, that he rent his garments.
And the king commanded Chilkiyah and Ahikam the son of Shafan and Abdon the son of Michah and Shafan the scribe and Asayah the king's servant, saying:

"Go, inquire of Havayah on my behalf and on behalf of those remaining in Yisroel and in Yehudah concerning the words of the scroll which has been found, for great is Havayah's wrath which has been poured upon us, since our forefathers did not keep the word of Havayah, to do according to all that is written in this scroll."

And Chilkiyah and those whom the king [sent] went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shalum the son of Tokhath the son of Hasrah, the keeper of the raiment, and she was sitting in Yerushalayim in the study-hall, and they spoke to her accordingly.
And she said to them, "So has Havayah Elokim of Yisroel said: Say to the man who sent you to me:
So Havayah said, 'Behold I bring calamity upon this place and upon its inhabitants — all the curses that are written in this scroll, which they read before the king of Yehudah.

Because they have forsaken Me and have burned incense to pagan deities, in order to provoke Me with all the deeds of their hands, My wrath is poured down upon this place, and it shall not be quenched.'
And concerning the king of Yehudah, who has sent you to inquire of Havayah, so shall you say to him: So has Havayah Elokim of Yisroel said, 'The words as you have heard.

Since your heart has become soft, and you have humbled yourself before Elokim when you heard His words about this place and about its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before Me and rent your garments and wept before Me, I, too, have heard [it],' Havayah says.

Therefore, behold I gather you to your forefathers, and you shall be gathered to your graves in peace, and your eyes shall not see any of the calamity that I am bringing upon this place and upon its inhabitants." And they brought back word to the king.
And the king summoned, and he assembled all the elders of Yehudah and Yerushalayim.

And the king went up to the House of Havayah, and all the people of Yehudah and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim were with him, and the priests and the Leviim, and all the people from great to small, and he read within their hearing all the words of the Scroll of the Covenant that was found in the House of Havayah.

And the king stood in his place, and enacted the covenant before Havayah, to follow Havayah and to observe His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to fulfill the words of the covenant, which were written in this scroll.
And he stood up all those found in Yerushalayim and Binyamin, and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim did according to the covenant of Elokim, the Elokim of their forefathers.

And Yoshiyah removed all the abominations from all the lands of the Children of Yisroel, and he caused all those found in Yisroel to serve, to serve Havayah their Elokim; all his days they did not turn away from following Havayah Elokim of their forefathers.
And Yoshiyah made the Passover sacrifice in Yerushalayim to Havayah, and they slaughtered the Passover sacrifice on the fourteenth day of the first month.
And he stationed the priests on their watches, and he encouraged them to the service of the House of Havayah.

And he said to the Leviim who taught all Yisroel, who were holy to Havayah, "Place the Holy Ark in the House that Shlomo the son of Dovid, the king of Yisroel, built; you have no burden on the shoulders; now serve Havayah your Elokim and His people Yisroel.
And prepare yourselves for your fathers' houses according to your divisions, according to the writing of Dovid king of Yisroel and according to the writing of Shlomo his son.
And stand in the Sanctuary according to the divisions of the fathers' houses of your brethren the members of the people, and [let there be for each] a division of the fathers' houses of the Leviim.
And slaughter the Passover sacrifice and sanctify yourselves and prepare your brethren to do according to the word of Havayah by the hand of Moshe."

And Yoshiyah separated for the members of the people-small cattle; lambs and young goats, all for the Passover sacrifices for all that were present, for the number of thirty thousand, and large cattle-three thousand; these were from the king's property.

And his officers separated for the people, for the priests, and for the Leviim. Chilkiyah, Zecharyah, and Yechiel, the rulers of the House of Elokim, gave the priests for the Passover sacrifices two thousand and six hundred [small cattle], and large cattle, three hundred.

And Conanyah and Shemayah and Nethanel his brethren, and Chashavyah the chiefs of the Leviim, separated for the Leviim for the Passover sacrifices five thousand [small cattle], and five hundred large cattle.
And the service was established, and the priests stood in their place and the Leviim in their divisions, according to the command of the king.
And they slaughtered the Passover sacrifice, and the priests sprinkled with their hand, and the Leviim were flaying.

And they removed the burnt-offerings to give them to the divisions of the fathers' houses of the members of the people to sacrifice to Havayah, as is written in the Book of Moshe, and so for the large cattle.

And they cooked the Passover sacrifice with fire according to the law, and the hallowed things they cooked in pots and in cauldrons and in pans and carried them quickly to all the members of the people.

And afterwards, they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aharon were [engaged] in offering up the burnt-offerings and the fats until night; and the Leviim prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aharon.

And the singers, the sons of Asaf were in their place according to the command of Dovid and Asaf and Heiman and Yedusun, the king's seer, and the gate sentries for each gate; there was no need for them to depart from their service, for their brethren the Leviim prepared for them.
And the service of Havayah was well established on that day, to perform the Passover sacrifice and to offer up burnt-offerings on the altar of Havayah, according to the command of King Yoshiyah.
And the Children of Yisroel who were present performed the Passover sacrifice at that time, and the Festival of Matzoth seven days.

And such a Passover sacrifice had not been made in Yisroel since the days of Shmuel the prophet; and neither did any of the kings of Yisroel make such a Passover as Yoshiyah did, and the priests, the Leviim, and all of Yehudah and Yisroel that were present, and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Yoshiyah, this Passover sacrifice was made.
After all this, that Yoshiyah had prepared the Temple, Neco, the king of Mitzrayim, went up to wage war in Carchemish on the Peras, and Yoshiyah went forth toward him.

And he sent messengers to him, saying, "What have I to do with you, king of Yehudah? Not against you yourself [do I go] today, but to my place of war, and Elokim said to hasten me. Desist from the Elokim who is with me, and he will not destroy you."

But Yoshiyah did not turn his face away from him, but he disguised himself to wage war with him, and he did not hearken to the words of Neco from the mouth of Elokim, and he came to wage war in the valley of Megiddo.
And the archers shot at King Yoshiyah, and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am sorely stricken!"

And his servants took him away from the chariot, and they put him into his second chariot and brought him to Yerushalayim, and he died and was buried in the graves of his forefathers, and all of Yehudah and Yerushalayim were mourning for Yoshiyah.

And Yirmeyah lamented Yoshiyah, and all the male and female singers spoke of Yoshiyah in their lamentations until this day, and they made them a statute over Yisroel, and behold, they are written in the lamentations.
And the rest of the affairs of Yoshiyah and his kind deeds, as are written in the Law of Havayah.
And his early and late affairs-behold they are written in the book of the kings of Yisroel and Yehudah.
And the people of the land took Yehoachaz the son of Yoshiyah and made him king instead of his father in Yerushalayim.
Yehoachaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Yerushalayim.
And the king of Mitzrayim deposed him in Yerushalayim, and he imposed a fine upon the land of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
And the king of Mitzrayim crowned Elyakim his brother over Yehudah and Yerushalayim, and he changed his name to Yehoyakim, and Neco took Yoahaz his brother and brought him to Mitzrayim.
Yehoyakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim, and he did that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah his Elokim.
Nevuchadnezzar the king of Bavel advanced upon him, and bound him in copper chains to bring him to Bavel.
And Nevuchadnezzar brought some of the vessels of the House of Havayah to Bavel and placed them in his palace in Bavel.

And the rest of the affairs of Yehoyakim and the abominations which he committed, and that which was found upon him-behold they are written in the book of the kings of Yisroel and Yehudah, and Yehoyachin his son reigned in his stead.
Yehoyachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Yerushalayim, and he did that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah.

And at the return of the year, King Nevuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Bavel with the precious vessels of the House of Havayah, and he made Tzidkiyah his brother king over Yehudah and Yerushalayim.
Tzidkiyah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim.
And he did that which was evil in the eyes of Havayah his Elokim; he did not humble himself before Yirmeyah the prophet, [speaking] from the mouth of Havayah.
And he also rebelled against King Nevuchadnezzar, who adjured him by Elokim, and he stiffened his neck and strengthened his heart, not to return to Havayah Elokim of Yisroel.

Also, all the chiefs of the priests and the people committed many treacherous acts, like all the abominations of the nations, and they defiled the House of Havayah, which He had hallowed in Yerushalayim.
And Havayah Elokim of their forefathers sent upon them through His messengers, sending them early and often, for He had pity on His people and on His abode.
But they mocked the messengers of Elokim, and despised His words and scoffed His prophets, until Havayah's wrath ascended upon His people beyond remedy.

And He brought upon them the king of the Kasdim, and he slew their young men by the sword in their Temple, and he had pity neither on youth nor virgin, elder nor ancient one; He delivered all into his hand.
And all the vessels of the House of Elokim, both large and small, and the treasuries of the House of Havayah, and the treasuries of the king and his officers; he brought everything to Bavel.
And they burned the House of Elokim, and they demolished the wall of Yerushalayim, and all its palaces they burned with fire, and destroyed all its precious vessels.
And he exiled the survivors from the sword to Bavel, and they became vassals to him and to his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Paras.
To fulfill the word of Havayah in the mouth of Yirmeyah, until the land was appeased for its Sabbaths; [for] all the days of its desolation it rested until the completion of seventy years.

And in the first year of Koresh, king of Paras, at the completion of the word of Havayah in the mouth of Yirmeyah, Havayah aroused the spirit of Koresh the king of Paras, and he issued a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying:

"So Koresh said the king of Paras: All the kingdoms of the earth has Havayah Elokim of the heavens delivered to me, and He commanded me to build Him a House in Yerushalayim, which is in Yehudah. Who among you is of all His people, may Havayah his Elokim be with him, and he may ascend."
